Wider Sports News.title: Disney+ continues to move into live sport – but what role will it play in the streamer’s global future?
Wider Sports News.summary: Over the past 18 months, Disney+ has steadily grown its live sport offering for users outside the US. Yet between a patchwork of local and global deals, and a series of experiments with formats and its own venerated IP, its strategy is perhaps still to fully emerge. The post Disney+ continues to move into live sport – but what role will it play in the streamer’s global future? appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
Back in April, ESPN arrived on Disney+ across 53 countries and territories in Europe and the Asia-Pacific region. Users could now find live and on-demand sport in a tab at the top of their screen – alongside content from Marvel, Star Wars, Pixar and Hulu. For a seven-year-old streamer built on the world’s most familiar entertainment IP, this was a clear indication that sport will become a bigger part of its offer.

Those signals have kept coming. Last week, Disney+ confirmed a five-year deal with the National Hockey League (NHL) for live streaming rights in Sweden and Finland, two of the biggest ice hockey markets in Europe.

Wider Sports News.title: ‘A really trusted asset class’: Why Palace and Newcastle’s shirt sponsors are backing the Premier League’s post-betting era
Wider Sports News.summary: The CMOs of Crystal Palace partner Temporal and Newcastle United backer Knox Hydrate explain how Premier League shirt sponsorship is opening new doors for their brands – and delivering more value than other marketing channels could. The post ‘A really trusted asset class’: Why Palace and Newcastle’s shirt sponsors are backing the Premier League’s post-betting era appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
The Premier League has just undergone its most visible commercial shift in a generation. Ahead of the 2026/27 season, more than half of English soccer’s top-flight teams were seeking brands to appear on the front of their matchday jerseys. In most cases, that prestigious slot had been vacated by a betting company.

A voluntary collective ban on front-of-shirt gambling sponsorship, which went into effect over the summer, has triggered a new wave of commercial dynamics. Betting brands were typically willing to pay a considerable premium for the international platform that Premier League shirt deals presented. For middle and lower-ranking clubs in a fiercely competitive division, the financial implications of that were impossible to overlook.

Wider Sports News.body:
London, UK 17th September 2026 – The LTA has appointed Two Circles as its social media partner through to the end of 2028, as the organisation looks to accelerate audience growth, deepen fan engagement and expand the impact of its digital content strategy.

Under the multi-year agreement, Two Circles will support the LTA across strategic social and content planning, creative production, channel management, insights and reporting, paid media support and social media monetisation. The partnership will focus on strengthening the LTA’s connection with tennis fans, inspiring participation through engagement and driving commercial growth.

Wider Sports News.title: French soccer’s DTC dilemma: Why the LFP’s rights tender doesn’t mean the end of Ligue 1+
Wider Sports News.summary: With Ligue 1 reportedly set to resume talks over the next domestic rights cycle, Cyprien Castanedo, head of media platform and innovation at the LFP, explains why Ligue 1+ still has a part to play. The post French soccer’s DTC dilemma: Why the LFP’s rights tender doesn’t mean the end of Ligue 1+ appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
A year ago, Ligue 1 became the first major European soccer league to go almost entirely direct-to-consumer (DTC) in its home market with the launch of Ligue 1+. It was a groundbreaking move watched closely by the entire industry. But it was also an act of necessity, with the French Professional League (LFP) suffering from a collapse of the conventional market for its rights.

The early signs were encouraging, with a million subscribers signing up in the first month. Yet the future of Ligue 1’s great streaming experiment remains uncertain, with the LFP possibly planning for life after Ligue 1+ – at least as a primary distribution platform – already.

The post ‘Digitisation is the new asset class’: Genius Sports CEO on how media fragmentation is transforming sport’s monetisation model appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
When Genius Sports was founded in 2001 the dotcom crash was in full swing, betting was still predominantly an analogue activity done in high street shops, and the use of data within sport was a niche activity pursued exclusively by enthusiasts and outsiders.

The digitisation of sport and society over the subsequent quarter of a century has transformed everything. Data analytics are present in virtually every sporting activity and technology is a key driver of growth and efficiency in the professional arena.

Rugby.title: Bears pair Staddon and Heward suffer ACL injuries
Rugby.summary: Bristol Bears pair Ethan Staddon and Noah Heward suffer ACL injuries while Kalaveti Ravouvou is out for 12 weeks with a knee injury.
Rugby.body:
New Bristol Bears signing Ethan Staddon and back Noah Heward have both suffered anterior cruciate ligament injuries and face long spells on the sidelines. Staddon was Bristol's most high-profile signing this summer, with the versatile back-row forward making the move from neighbours Bath.

However he has already undergone surgery, as has Heward, who went off five minutes into the team's Prem Rugby Cup loss to Exeter two weeks ago. Centre Kalaveti Ravouvou is also unavailable for around 12 weeks after picking up a knee injury while on international duty with Fiji, and is unlikely to feature until after the November international break.

Rugby.title: Tigers looking to evolve
Rugby.summary: Head coach Geoff Parling says Leicester Tigers need to keep "evolving" in their constant pursuit of silverware.
Rugby.body:
Head coach Geoff Parling says Leicester Tigers need to keep "evolving" in their constant pursuit of silverware. The East Midlands club finished fourth in the Prem table and were beaten in the semi-finals of the competition in Parling's first season in charge last term.

Tigers did, however, win the Prem Cup and reached the last 16 of the European Champions Cup – where they were beaten 64-14 by eventually title winners Bordeaux Begles. Leicester start their league campaign against Saracens on Sunday, and while Parling said this season's aims had "not been discussed" he admits the aspirations of English rugby's most decorated side is inescapable.

Rugby.title: ‘South Africa has produced enough URC finalists. This season it needs a champion’
Rugby.summary: A case could be made for all four South African teams reaching the play-offs this season, but each has points to prove with RWC places on the line.
Rugby.body:
One URC title in five completed seasons is a poor return for four teams that provide the domestic spine of the Springboks and have occupied six of the competition’s 10 final places.

The Stormers won the inaugural title in 2022. Since then, South African sides have reached four successive finals and lost them all. The Bulls have been runners-up in the last three, twice against Leinster and once against Glasgow. South Africa has been the URC’s most reliable finalist and its least successful champion.

Rugby.title: Ex-Welsh first minister Jones joins Scarlets board
Rugby.summary: New Scarlets board member Carwyn Jones says Welsh rugby needs four professional teams as the threat of closure looms.
Rugby.body:
Former Welsh first minister Carwyn Jones is to join Scarlets' board during a season in which their long-term future is under threat. Jones served as Wales' top politician between 2009 and 2018 and has since become a peer with the title Lord Jones of Penybont.

Born in Swansea, Jones attended Aberystwyth University, where he played rugby, before serving as a member of the Senedd for Bridgend for more than 20 years. Under Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) plans, Scarlets and Swansea-based Ospreys are rivals to remain as one of a three-team professional tier in Wales beyond 2028.

Rugby.title: Rugby player's murder trial: Sentences of 20 and 27 years sought by prosecutors
Rugby.summary: The trial concerning the murder of former Pumas international Federico Martín Aramburú, who was fatally shot on March 19, 2022, has reached a new stage...
Rugby.body:
The trial concerning the killing of former Pumas international Federico Martín Aramburú, who was fatally shot on March 19, 2022, has reached a new stage, with the attorney general in charge of the case seeking sentences of 27 and 20 years for the two defendants.

Philippe Courroye, the lead prosecutor in the case, is seeking convictions that would see Loïk Le Priol and Romain Bouvier behind bars, accusing both men of carrying out a premeditated killing.

Rugby.title: Glasgow Warriors pick 11 Scotland internationals for trip to Munster
Rugby.summary: Glasgow have selected a strong team featuring 11 Scotland internationals for their opening United Rugby Championship against Munster at Thomond Park on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
Glasgow Warriors have selected a strong team featuring 11 Scotland internationals for their opening United Rugby Championship against Munster at Thomond Park on Saturday. Hooker Gregor Hiddleston, who won his first three Test caps in the Scots’ opening Nations Championship fixtures in July, starts in the front row along with tighthead Murphy Walker, with Gregor Brown and Max Williamson packing down at lock.

Rory Darge and Matt Fagerson feature in the back row, the latter reverting from blindside to his former No.8 role after the departure of Jack Dempsey to Japan. The back three features Kyle Rowe and Jamie Dobie – making his 100th Warriors appearance – on the wings alongside soon-to-be-Scottish-qualified full-back Josh McKay, with captain Stafford McDowall and Ollie Smith teaming up at centre and George Horne starting at scrum-half alongside Dan Lancaster at No.10.

Porter’s move across the front row has been the subject of speculation for some time, but Cullen has now opted to make it a reality as Leinster begin a new campaign in Johannesburg.

Rugby.title: Canada rest Sophie de Goede for France clash in La Rochelle
Rugby.summary: Canada captain Sophie de Goede has been rested for her team's WXV Global Series encounter with France in La Rochelle.
Rugby.body:
Canada captain Sophie de Goede has been rested for her team’s WXV Global Series encounter with France in La Rochelle. The lock forward played the full 80 minutes of her team’s 26-26 draw with England last time out.

She has been left out of the squad after coaching staff opted to rest certain players ahead of their home fixtures against the Red Roses in October. Instead, Rachel Smith will partner Laetitia Royer in the second row.

Rugby.title: McLachlan and Wills return to face Australia
Rugby.summary: Rachel McLachlan and Evie Wills return from injury to start for Scotland against Australia in their final home match of the WXV Series on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
Rachel McLachlan and Evie Wills return from injury to start for Scotland against Australia in their final home match of the WXV Series on Saturday. Sarah Bonar and Hannah Ramsay also come into the starting line-up as interim head coach Dave Butcher makes four changes following the 66-14 defeat by New Zealand.

Butcher believes facing Canada and New Zealand has helped the development of his team despite suffering two heavy defeats. "Coming out of two really, really hard games, the feeling is that we got stress tested a lot in those games, which has allowed us to accelerate what we need to do a little bit more, rather than playing a game where we're not too sure whether that will work against the world's best," he said.

Rugby.title: Scotland and Edinburgh suffer brutal Darcy Graham blow on eve of season
Rugby.summary: Edinburgh wing Darcy Graham will miss at least the first three months of the season including Scotland’s Nations Championship campaign in November after suffering a “freakish” injury on the eve of the new campaign.
Rugby.body:
Edinburgh wing Darcy Graham will miss at least the first three months of the season including Scotland’s Nations Championship campaign in November after suffering a “freakish” injury on the eve of the new campaign.

The 29-year-old flyer suffered a “contusion on his bicep” during Edinburgh’s pre-season friendly at Harlequins last Friday, his first game of the season. A subsequent MRI scan revealed Graham has ruptured a bicep muscle in his arm and is likely to be sidelined until Christmas.

Rugby.title: Injury rules Graham out of Scotland's autumn Tests
Rugby.summary: Scotland's record try-scorer Darcy Graham is to miss the autumn internationals against New Zealand, Australia and Japan with a ruptured bicep.
Rugby.body:
Scotland's record try-scorer Darcy Graham is to miss the autumn internationals with a bicep injury. The 29-year-old Edinburgh winger has 38 tries from his 57 caps but will not have the chance to add to that tally in home Tests against New Zealand, Australia and Japan.

Edinburgh head coach Sean Everitt revealed Graham is facing at least 12 weeks on the sidelines as he recovers from a rupture. Describing the collision incident as "pretty freakish", Everitt, said: "That's not good news for us and not good news for him, especially with the autumn series coming up."

Rugby.title: Feaunati returns as England brace for Black Ferns onslaught
Rugby.summary: Maddie Feaunati returns to bring big-game experience and dynamism to the back row as England take on a resurgent New Zealand at Allianz Stadium on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
Maddie Feaunati returns to bring big-game experience and dynamism to the back row as England take on a resurgent New Zealand, their closest challengers at the top of the world rankings, in front of more than 50,000 fans at Allianz Stadium on Saturday.

Feaunati comes in at number eight, with Alex Matthews shifting to blind-side flanker and Abi Burton to the bench. The three starters all featured in England's Women's Rugby World Cup final win against Canada, one year ago on Sunday.

Rugby.summary: Harlequins are without injured George Furbank and Marcus Smith for Friday's Prem opener but Bath's have Will Stuart back in their XV, while Newcastle start seven new signings.
Rugby.body:
The first round of the Prem returns this weekend with all 10 teams starting with a clean slate as the new season begins. This is the first chance for fans to see new signings in their club colours and whether the summer break and pre-season training block has created a fresh impetus in their teams.

Rugby.summary: Red Roses boss John Mitchell has made three changes to his starting XV to face the Black Ferns at Allianz Stadium.
Rugby.body:
Red Roses boss John Mitchell has made three changes to his starting XV to face the Black Ferns at Allianz Stadium. The changes include starts for prop duo Mackenzie Carson and Sarah Bern, who join Bryony Field in the front row. Field earns her second consecutive Test start, while Lilli Ives Campion and Morwenna Talling form the second-row partnership.

Maddie Feaunati also returns to the starting line-up after making a strong impact from the bench in England’s 26-26 draw with Canada last week. Her inclusion at No. 8 sees Alex Matthews move to blindside flanker, with Sadia Kabeya completing the back row at openside flanker.

Rugby.summary: Scotland interim head coach Dave Butcher has made four changes to his starting XV for Australia's visit to Edinburgh.
Rugby.body:
Scotland interim head coach Dave Butcher has made four changes to his starting XV for Australia’s visit to Edinburgh. Two of these changes are enforced. A wrist injury has ruled second row Emma Wassell out for 10 weeks, meaning Sarah Bonar has been parachuted into the second row to partner Holland Bogan.

With Rachel Philipps out with concussion, Evie Wills is installed at centre to partner Meryl Smith. There is also a place for Hannah Ramsay who, after outings from the bench against Canada and New Zealand, starts at full-back ahead of Chloe Rollie.

Rugby.title: Henry Pollock signs off momentous week with a milestone
Rugby.summary: Henry Pollock will make his 50th Northampton Saints appearance on Friday night as the PREM champions open their season against Newcastle Red Bulls at DPD Stadium at Franklin’s Gardens.
Rugby.body:
Henry Pollock will make his 50th Northampton Saints appearance on Friday night as the PREM champions open their season against Newcastle Red Bulls at DPD Stadium at Franklin’s Gardens.

The 21-year-old reaches the landmark days after signing a new contract, capping a big week for the back-rower as he begins his fifth season at the club. Pollock starts at openside alongside Josh Kemeny and former Newcastle captain Callum Chick, with Alex Coles and Ed Prowse in the second-row. They will line up against former Saint Sam Graham in the back-row, who made the move north over the summer.

Rugby.title: Who will be the Gallagher Prem signings of the season?
Rugby.summary: As a new Gallagher Prem season begins, RugbyPass picks out the new - and returning - faces who are set to impress most this campaign.
Rugby.body:
England’s directors of rugby have generally agreed this past transfer season was the most bonkers the Gallagher Prem has seen. Top internationals have switched clubs within the league, while the strengthening of Newcastle’s long flimsy financial muscle has added more upheaval to the mix.

Here, RugbyPass selects the best recruits for the season ahead. Red Bull’s investment is being realised in a major way, with over 20 new players arriving at Kingston Park, many of them with international pedigree. Raffi Quirke is a huge acquisition. Pouri Rakete-Stones and Werner Kok will become fan favourites in the front-row and on the wing. Others, such as Franco Molina, Sam Graham, Will Rigg, Rusi Tuima and Allan Ferrie will be effective in more understated fashion. If his move goes through, record-breaking Super Rugby try-scorer and recent All Black debutant Fehi Fineanganofo should be a serious hit.

Rugby.title: From ruin to a (Red) Bull market
Rugby.summary: Prem Rugby seemed on the brink of disaster after Worcester, Wasps and London Irish went bust, but there is renewed confidence and fresh money in the league.
Rugby.body:
Simon Massie-Taylor pulled up outside Newcastle's Kingston Park stadium, and saw fear. The unannounced arrival of Prem Rugby's chief executive at one of the league's clubs had rarely been a good sign.

Massie-Taylor started the role in January 2022. In the 18 months that followed, Wasps, Worcester and London Irish, with finances stretched out of shape by Covid, had flamed out of the English top flight.

Rugby.title: Carys Cox Boost for Wales Ahead of WXV Clash with USA in Cardiff
Rugby.summary: Carys Cox has returned to Wales' starting side for their WXV Global Series clash with the USA Women's Eagles on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
Carys Cox has returned to Wales’ starting side for their WXV Global Series clash with the USA Women’s Eagles on Saturday. It will be the 27-year-old’s first appearance since she started in Trailfinders Women’s Premiership Women’s Rugby final loss against Saracens. Injury meant that Cox missed Wales’ 50-19 win against the Springbok Women last Friday night. She joins Amy Williams and Lisa Neumann to add to an already potent back three.

Head coach, Sean Lynn, has not changed the pack for the visit of the USA, who stunned Ireland with a second half comeback on Sunday to register a 40-36 win in Dublin. Lock forward Georgia Evans will start in the engine room on the occasion of her 50th Test match for Wales. She partners Branwen Metcalfe.

Rugby.title: Gloucester's PREM rivals ready to swoop for England centre Seb Atkinson
Rugby.summary: Leicester Tigers are understood to be exploring a potential move for Gloucester inside centre Seb Atkinson when his contract runs out at the end of the season.
Rugby.body:
Leicester Tigers are understood to be exploring a potential move for Gloucester inside centre Seb Atkinson when his contract runs out at the end of the season. The Tigers believe Atkinson, 24, who has won seven England caps, could address one of their squad’s problem areas next season and have put him on a list of players they are keen to speak to.

Atkinson, who started his career at Worcester Warriors, joined Gloucester in 2022, won a PREM Rugby Cup two years later, and was linked with a move to London, where his girlfriend, Siena, works for Goldman Sachs.

Rugby.title: 'Expectations are so high at Leinster that merely league-winning seasons are not considered good enough'
Rugby.summary: Leinster are expected to lead the charge of Irish provinces but it's Connacht who are expected to exceed expectations, with fears for Munster
Rugby.body:
The milk and honey transfer days of Jordie Barrett, Damien de Allende, Brad Thorn, Ruan Pienaar, Christian Cullen, Isa Nacewa, Mils Muliaina and Duane Vermeulen are behind us. Ireland’s four professional teams are no longer focusing on marquee signings from abroad. Instead, they are either tempting Irish players to jump provinces, repatriating old boys, or relying on scouts to find relatively cheap gems.

Earlier this month, the Irish Rugby Football Union announced it was seeking expressions of interest for a partner to design, build, finance and operate ‘Lansdowne Quarter’ – a large hotel and apartment complex, located right across the road from Aviva Stadium.

Rugby.title: The URC stat Leinster and Stormers were neck-to-neck on
Rugby.summary: Five seasons into the BKT United Rugby Championship, the competition continues to deliver a compelling mix of speed, variety and contrasting rugby identities.
Rugby.body:
Five seasons into the BKT United Rugby Championship, the competition continues to deliver a compelling mix of speed, variety and contrasting rugby identities. The latest numbers show a league playing with greater attacking ambition than ever: BKT URC 5 (25/26 season) produced an average of 6.9 tries per match, with a try scored every 363.5 seconds—the fastest rate across the five seasons.

From Glasgow Warriors’ high-tempo attacking game to the power of the Vodacom Bulls, the set-piece threat of the DHL Stormers and the clinical efficiency of Leinster Rugby, the BKT URC offers multiple ways to win.

Rugby.title: Zachary Porthen joins growing Bok chorus as questions linger
Rugby.summary: South Africa tighthead prop Zachary Porthen has reiterated the message that has been coming out of the Springboks camp this week, saying the squad are "hungrier than you might think."
Rugby.body:
South Africa tighthead prop Zachary Porthen has reiterated the message that has been coming out of the Springboks camp this week, saying the squad are “hungrier than you might think.”

The Boks take on Australia in Perth on Sunday just two weeks after securing a 3-1 series win over the All Blacks in Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry. Rassie Erasmus has made 13 changes to the XV that ran out in the fourth Test in Baltimore, with only Eben Etzebeth and Ethan Hooker retaining their places, leading to concerns that the world champions may falter after such an intense schedule.

Rugby.summary: Michaela Leonard will become the first player to reach 50 Test caps for the Wallaroos when she starts against Scotland in Edinburgh this weekend.
Rugby.body:
Michaela Leonard will become the first player to reach 50 Test caps for the Wallaroos when she starts against Scotland in Edinburgh this weekend. The lock, who became the most-capped Australian woman in April, has featured in 49 of the 102 Wallaroos Test matches that have been played since 1994.

She starts in the second row alongside Kaitlan Leaney as Australia look for their first win of WXV Global Series 2026. In total five changes have been made to the matchday 23 that was beaten 29-26 by France a week ago in Aix-en-Provence.

Rugby.title: URC preview: Judgement looms for Everitt and Edinburgh as Glasgow place faith in 'the young team'
Rugby.summary: Despite his team's poor form, Sean Everitt has been backed to overhaul Edinburgh while Glasgow's Franco Smith looks to take his increasingly young squad further.
Rugby.body:
The clatter of studs echoes down the tunnel, and the tang of Deep Heat lingers in the air. Two months after an unrelenting hamster wheel of a season juddered to a halt, the competitive stuff returns. For Scotland’s Lions, the campaign began in June last year with the warm-up fixture against Argentina, and ended 13 months later with three games in the newly minted Nations Championship. Ben White played 33 matches in that time and has already featured in three more for Toulon. Sione Tuipulotu played 36 games, Kyle Steyn and Stafford McDowall 30. Pierre Schoeman was involved in 32, before being reintegrated into domestic training during the first week of September.

What will Schoeman have found on his return to Edinburgh? Sean Everitt has conducted a radical overhaul of the club which, while rough on those leaving, felt wholly necessary. New coaches, new staff, new philosophy. The plan has been brewing for many months, and was cemented during the negotiation of his two-year contract extension. The buzzwords are “fight, care and grow”. Since the early days of Mike Blair’s reign, there has not been anywhere near enough of the latter.

Rugby.title: Baxter targeting Prem title win with Exeter
Rugby.summary: Exeter boss Rob Baxter says his side has to target winning the Prem title this season.
Rugby.body:
Exeter Chiefs director of rugby Rob Baxter says his side has to target winning the Prem title this season. The Chiefs surprised many by making last season's Prem final, having finished second-from-bottom in the 2024-25 campaign.

Baxter's side finished third last season and won a dramatic semi-final at Bath before being beaten in the final at Twickenham by Northampton. "I genuinely think that you've got a target winning the Premiership if you've lost the final, I just think you have to," Baxter said.

Rugby.summary: BBC Sport Wales looks at the prospects for Cardiff, Dragons, Ospreys and Scarlets in the 2026-27 United Rugby Championship season.
Rugby.body:
Perhaps it is down to the hope and excitement of pre-season but all four Welsh clubs go into the 2026-27 United Rugby Championship (URC) with dreams of making the play-offs. Last season Cardiff were the only side from Wales to make the top eight while Scarlets and Ospreys were the sole Welsh representatives in 2025 and 2024 respectively.

Those three, and Dragons, have shown they can mix it with the best in the league on their day and all will feel the top eight is not out of reach if they have some luck with injury.

Rugby.title: Steve Hansen: Veteran Boks might call it quits on Erasmus ahead of 2027
Rugby.summary: Former All Blacks head coach Steve Hansen has warned Rassie Erasmus that some veteran players may call it quits ahead of the 2027 Rugby World Cup.
Rugby.body:
Former All Blacks head coach Steve Hansen has warned Rassie Erasmus that some veteran players may call it quits ahead of the 2027 Rugby World Cup. Speaking from experience after the 2015 Rugby World Cup title, Hansen said that the coaches were very aware of the age profile of their team heading into 2019.

The Springboks are carrying a number of veterans from the double World Cup wins such as Eben Etzebeth, Siya Kolisi, Pieter-steph du Toit, Jesse Kriel, and Cheslin Kolbe. “We had a group of players heading into 2015 who were getting on the older side, and we had a discussion one by one with them about what they controlled,” Hansen said on the Rugby Unity and For the Love of Rugby SA podcast colloboration.

Rugby.title: Canada star’s immediate reaction to thrilling win over USA Eagles
Rugby.summary: Ben LeSage went to the 2019 Rugby World Cup and has played more than 70 Tests in Canadian red.
Rugby.body:
Ben LeSage went to the 2019 Rugby World Cup and has played more than 70 Tests in Canadian red, but last weekend’s 19-16 win over the USA Eagles in a thrilling Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup showdown ranks right up there.

LeSage, who was the most experienced back in Canada’s squad for the Pacific Nations Cup, set the tone early with a moment of individual brilliance. Front-rower Foster Dewitt linked up with the red headgear-wearing centre, who raced away for the first try of the third-place playoff.

Rugby.title: Ex-All Black captain Barrett named to play for first time in 10 months
Rugby.summary: Former All Black captain Scott Barrett will play for Taranaki this weekend marking his first game of professional rugby in 10 months.
Rugby.body:
Former All Black captain Scott Barrett will play for Taranaki this weekend marking his first game of professional rugby in 10 months. The 32-year-old will make just his second appearance ever for the Bulls when they play Hawke’s Bay in Napier.

Barrett had surgery only months ago, a discectomy to treat a bulging disc which caused issues for the left side of his body. “[The injury] depowered my left side so I couldn’t really run and do the things required for my job as a rugby player so yeah, it’s nice to be in a position to pull on the jersey and represent Taranaki again,” he told 1 News.

Rugby.title: Kaipo Olsen-Baker returns for Black Ferns ahead of Red Roses blockbuster
Rugby.summary: Kaipo Olsen-Baker is back in action and has been named in the Black Ferns’ starting XV for their Test against the Red Roses on Saturday 26 September.
Rugby.body:
Kaipo Olsen-Baker is back in action and has been named in the Black Ferns’ starting XV for their Test against the Red Roses on Saturday 26 September. With over 50,000 fans expected at Allianz Stadium for the clash between the fierce rivals, the Black Ferns’ final Test of the WXV Global Series in the Northern Hemisphere promises to deliver some blockbuster entertainment.

Black Ferns head coach Whitney Hansen has named her match-day 23, which sees the return of Olsen-Baker, winger Ayesha Leti-I’iga and lock Laura Bayfield, and after overpowering Scotland in a ten-try 66-14 victory at Hive Stadium in Edinburgh, the side will be looking to continue their 100 per cent win record under her leadership.

Rugby.title: Marlie Packer and Red Roses want Test rugby bar to ‘keep raising’
Rugby.summary: Marlie Packer is not interested in easy wins. The most capped member of John Mitchell’s current Red Roses squad wants the side to be pushed, tested and forced to find another gear.
Rugby.body:
Marlie Packer is not interested in easy wins. The most-capped member of John Mitchell’s current Red Roses squad wants the side to be pushed, tested and forced to find another gear – and that is exactly what she believes is happening as the women’s game continues to grow.

After England’s 39-match winning run was halted by Canada in an emphatic 26-26 draw at Sandy Park in the WXV Global Series, the 36-year-old flanker insists there was plenty to take from the contest.

Rugby.title: Maia Roos: Black Ferns ready to go to ‘dark places’ against Red Roses
Rugby.summary: Maia Roos, Santo Taumata, Georgia Ponsonby, Ruahei Demant and Ayesha Leti-I'iga are the only players in the current Black Ferns squad to have beaten England in a Test match.
Rugby.body:
Maia Roos, Santo Taumata, Georgia Ponsonby, Ruahei Demant and Ayesha Leti-I’iga are the only players in the current Black Ferns squad to have beaten England in a Test match. On 12 November 2022, in the Women Rugby World Cup final at Eden Park, the Black Ferns won a glorious 34-31 upset of the Red Roses, who had won a world record 30 consecutive Test matches.

Roos started the final and was later nominated for World Rugby Breakthrough Player of the Year for her performances at the tournament. Three times in six matches she topped the Black Ferns tackle count. Additionally, she scored tries in pool wins against Wales [56-12] and Scotland [57-0] and helped the Black Ferns win 46 out of 53 of their own lineout throws.

Rugby.title: Dowson outlines return for ‘frustrated’ England prop Trevor Davison
Rugby.summary: Northampton Saints boss Phil Dowson has revealed that the club sent England tighthead Trevor Davison to Texas to help with his return to action after three operations on the knee injury he suffered earlier this year.
Rugby.body:
Northampton Saints boss Phil Dowson has revealed that the club sent England tighthead Trevor Davison to Texas to help with his return to action after three operations on the knee injury he suffered earlier this year.

Dowson hopes that Davison, 34, who was injured in the Gallagher PREM victory over Saracens at the end of March, will be back in action in October. He said that Davison, who has been capped eight times by England, is now back running with the physios, who will have the final say on when he can step up his workload before returning to action.

Rugby.title: Former England full-back Mike Brown headhunted for new coaching role
Rugby.summary: Harlequins legend Brown, 41, has spent the last 10 months as Esher RFC's Sporting Director.
Rugby.body:
England’s most-capped full-back Mike Brown has been appointed as the Director of Rugby at Loughborough University, with his new role taking effect from January 2027. Harlequins legend Brown, 41, has spent the last 10 months as Esher RFC’s Sporting Director, leading the first XV, as well as being responsible for the other senior teams at the National 2 East (level 4) club.

He will continue in his present role until the turn of the year, before taking on his new challenge in the Midlands, which will see him oversee the strategic direction and commercial growth of men’s and women’s rugby.

Rugby.title: Wales suffer scrum-half Lockwood blow for USA Test
Rugby.summary: Scrum-half Seren Lockwood is out of Wales' second WXV Test, against USA, after failing a head injury assessment.
Rugby.body:
Scrum-half Seren Lockwood has been ruled out of Wales' second WXV Global Series fixture, against USA in Cardiff on Saturday, after failing a head injury assessment. Lockwood was taken off during the first half of Wales' eight-try victory over South Africa and is now going through World Rugby's return to play protocols.

It is a blow for Wales with Lockwood and Keira Bevan proving a promising half-back partnership in a new-look backline. Her absence paves the way for Lleucu George to return at 10, with Bevan reverting to her usual position of nine at Cardiff Arms Park.

Rugby.body:

Rugby.title: No doubt Quins will be better this season
Rugby.summary: Harlequins head Jason Gilmore says the club will get back on track in the 2026-27 campaign.
Rugby.body:
Harlequins head coach Jason Gilmore says there is "no doubt" the club will perform better in the Prem this season. Quins endured a disappointing 2025-26 campaign and finished ninth in the table - their lowest position for eight years.

But Gilmore says the club have been working hard behind the scenes to improve recruitment, style of play and skill levels by refreshing the playing and coaching staff. "We went through a lot of change last year and some tough times, so we feel like it's almost a new start for us," Gilmore told BBC Radio London before the season opener against Bath at The Stoop on Friday.

Rugby.title: ‘It was so special’: Freya Bell on her Wales breakthrough and grandmother’s dream
Rugby.summary: For Freya Bell, earning her first senior start for Wales against South Africa last Friday night was the culmination of a journey that began later than most.
Rugby.body:
For Freya Bell, earning her first senior start for Wales against South Africa last Friday night was the culmination of a journey that began later than most. “I was a bit of a late comer,” she admitted. “When I was younger, I kind of did every sport, but rugby.

“I grew up in a very sporty family, so I played football, netball, cricket, but my dad and my brother are massive rugby fans, so I just wanted to give it a go.” At 16, Bell decided to stick with rugby. What followed was a rapid rise through the Welsh pathway, but there was one person in particular who had always dreamed of seeing her represent Wales.

Rugby.summary: JJ Hanrahan’s experience will be invaluable to Munster this season, according to his former team-mate Simon Zebo, as Ireland fly-half Jack Crowley is likely to miss the first half of the season.
Rugby.body:
JJ Hanrahan’s experience will be invaluable to Munster this season, according to his former team-mate Simon Zebo, as Ireland fly-half Jack Crowley is likely to miss the first half of the season.

Rugby.summary: The DHL Stormers are celebrating the homecoming of a trio of Springboks superstars as they put the pressure on themselves to win the BKT URC title for a second time.
Rugby.body:
The DHL Stormers are celebrating the homecoming of a trio of Springboks superstars as they put the pressure on themselves to win the BKT URC title for a second time. They have welcomed back flanker Siya Kolisi, winger Cheslin Kolbe and tighthead prop Wilco Louw following spells with the Hollywoodbets Sharks, Tokyo Sungoliath and the Vodacom Bulls respectively.

As captain Ruhan Nel confirms, it’s a real triple boost for the ambitious Cape Town-based outfit. “It’s pretty well documented about their abilities as rugby players, but I think if you look at the humans we are getting back into our system, that’s actually the thing that stands out the most for me,” said the veteran centre.

Rugby.title: Uncapped 20-year-old gets Ashton's RWC backing despite England warning
Rugby.summary: Former England wing Chris Ashton has tipped 20-year-old Saracens wing Jack Bracken to make a late surge into the reckoning for Steve Borthwick's World Cup squad this season.
Rugby.body:
Former England wing Chris Ashton has tipped 20-year-old Saracens wing Jack Bracken to make a late surge into the reckoning for Steve Borthwick’s World Cup squad this season. The 2024 World Rugby Junior World Championship winner, and son of 2003 World Cup winner Kyran Bracken, is entering the new Gallagher PREM season off the back of a sensational pre-season, scoring a hat-trick in Saracens’ 96-42 PREM Rugby Cup win over Northampton Saints, and backing it up the following week with another hat-trick against Ampthill.

Of course, wing is no easy position to break into for English players currently. Perhaps after the back-row, it is the position in which Borthwick has the most options. As there is seldom wing cover on the bench, there are realistically only two wing spots in a matchday squad, so it is a devilish task to earn a place there, and perhaps even harder to keep that spot as Henry Arundell and Tom Roebuck have experienced over the past year.

As there is seldom wing cover on the bench, there are realistically only two wing spots in a matchday squad, so it is a devilish task to earn a place there, and perhaps even harder to keep that spot as Henry Arundell and Tom Roebuck have experienced over the past year.

Rugby.title: 'Rather rugby boots than gumboots'
Rugby.summary: Tonga hooker Samiuela Moli reflects on the path - via vineyards, building sites and the collapse of his former club - that has led him to a fresh start at Leicester Tigers.
Rugby.body:
Samiuela Moli is particular about the boots he wears. There is nothing necessarily special about the pair that the Leicester Tigers hooker puts on when he plays, but they are a constant reminder of the path it took, through vineyards and building sites, to establish a professional rugby career.

Just months ago, the Tonga international did not even know where he would be lacing up next when Super Rugby team Moana Pasifika went out of business., external So it was rather fitting that 27-year-old Moli was still clutching his white and yellow boots after training at Mattioli Woods Welford Road when he sat in the stands to talk about what his new start - more than 11,400 miles (18,300km) away from the club that collapsed - means to him.

Rugby.summary: Immanuel Feyi-Waboso could be one of England's stars at next summer's World Cup if he can keep fit this season, says Exeter boss Rob Baxter.
Rugby.body:
Immanuel Feyi-Waboso could be one of England's stars at next summer's World Cup if he can keep fit this season, says Exeter boss Rob Baxter. The 23-year-old winger helped the Chiefs reach last season's Prem final but he missed the Six Nations after suffering a hamstring injury in early February.

Feyi-Waboso also missed the final game of the Prem season and Exeter's play-off semi-final win at Bath after fracturing his jaw at Leicester at the end of May, although he returned to feature for Exeter at Twickenham and for England in their Nations Championship matches.

Rugby.title: Girls' rugby participation grows by 49% during four-year RFU project
Rugby.summary: The number of girls playing age-grade rugby at clubs in England has increased by 49% across the past four years.
Rugby.body:
The number of girls playing age-grade rugby at clubs in England has increased by 49% across the past four years. The governing body for the sport in England has published a report outlining the key results from Impact ‘25, the transformational Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 legacy programme delivered by the RFU in partnership with the UK Government, Sport England and UK Sport. The programme has seen a huge increase in women’s and girls’ participation.

Over four years, Impact ’25 saw over £14.55m of government funding invested between 2022 and March 2026. In this time, girls’ club participation grew 49%, from 18,000 to 26,800. 40,000 girls aged between 6 and 12 were introduced to rugby over the same period. Women’s participation at universities supported by funding has grown by 38%.

Rugby.summary: Rugby sevens is set to increase its footprint within Oceania, with the Solomon Islands looking to expand its program.
Rugby.body:
Rugby sevens is set to increase its footprint within Oceania, with the Solomon Islands looking to expand its program through a potential partnership with the United Kingdom. Rugby has been on the move within the island nation throughout 2026, with last weekend seeing the National Rugby 7s competition at Town Ground Rugby Stadium in Honiara, featuring both male and female teams in THE senior division, and a men’s high school division.

The competition saw several close contests, with Covenant Rugby Club defeating Islanders Rugby Club 12-7 in the men’s final, while Malaita Subi defeated New Georgia 22-17, the final score coming in the closing stages of the match.

Rugby.summary: Wales prop Corey Domachowski opens up on his mental health struggles and explains why he's now on the other side of the fence when Scarlets take on Cardiff this weekend.
Rugby.body:
After his struggles of the past couple of years, Corey Domachowski has recaptured his love for the game and is ready for a very special reunion. The Wales prop admits his “head was in the shed” as he was plagued by a series of injuries and he ended up putting on a front to mask his troubles.

But now he’s fit again and has regained his spark having embarked on a new challenge with the Scarlets. As fate would have it, he faces an immediate showdown against his former team, with Cardiff Rugby the opponents in Llanelli this Saturday on the opening weekend of the BKT URC season.

Rugby.title: Rochelle Martin: 'Test rugby is pressure, but it filled my cup'
Rugby.summary: Rochelle Martin is the 180th inductee into the World Rugby Hall of Fame. Between 1994 and 2006, the uncompromising flanker played 32 Tests for the Black Ferns, winning 31 times and scoring 14 tries.
Rugby.body:
Rochelle Martin is the 180th inductee into the World Rugby Hall of Fame. Between 1994 and 2006, the uncompromising flanker played 32 Tests for the Black Ferns, winning 31 times and scoring 14 tries.

A member of the 1998, 2002 and 2006 Women’s Rugby World Cup-winning teams, she was never better than in the 2006 semi-final against France in Edmonton. The Black Ferns won 40-10, as Martin scoring two tries against the reigning Women’s Six Nations Grand Slam champions who had won 18 consecutive Tests.

Rugby.summary: Head coach Dan McFarland is excited to have the backing of Newcastle Red Bulls' owners as he tries to fuse a new team together in the Prem this season.
Rugby.body:
It is all change at Newcastle Red Bulls as they prepare for the new Prem season, but they plan to tackle it with the sort of fearless approach for which their owners are renowned.

With Red Bull taking over at Kingston Park in August 2025, it was a scramble to get things in place for last season. As a result, Newcastle could not bridge the gap to the other nine teams and finished bottom for a fourth successive campaign, with just two wins in 18 games.

Rugby.summary: Lancaster, who turns 57 early next month, is in the final year of his two-year contract as head coach of Connacht.
Rugby.body:
Former England head coach Stuart Lancaster has quickly dismissed rumours that he might be heading back to Leinster. Lancaster, who turns 57 early next month, is in the final year of his two-year contract as head coach of Connacht and has been linked in the media as a possible successor to Leo Cullen at Leinster. Cullen is to leave the province at the end of the season.

Cumbrian-born Lancaster was Cullen’s right-hand man during a trophy-laden spell at Leinster, which helped him to rebuild his coaching reputation after England’s early exit from the 2015 World Cup.

Rugby.title: Rupert Cox column: Ultimate Sevens is fresh, fast and full of potential
Rugby.summary: Ultimate Sevens: fast rugby, new laws and loads of fun, but where will it fit in the Sevens Rugby landscape?
Rugby.body:
Ultimate Sevens: fast rugby, new laws and loads of fun, but where will it fit in the Sevens Rugby landscape? Commentator Rupert Cox takes a look. Brand-spanking-new, ambitious and shiny, Ultimate Sevens lands in London this week for its first ever Grand Final at the GTech Stadium in Brentford. I’ll be back on the mic – I got hooked on Sevens in 2009 while working for Sky Sports, and have been round the world broadcasting on it ever since. At every level, Olympics to SVNS Series to invitational tournaments, Sevens brings excitement, speed, and so much talent, in a way quite different to Fifteens —and in a way that is very often underrated on the global stage.

So what of this glitzy new form of the game? Ultimate boasts the world’s biggest gathering of star players outside the World Series and Olympics, with over a hundred elite athletes jetting in from across the globe to compete in Cardiff, Biarritz and London. Teams are made up of Olympic gold medallists, world champions and SVNS Series legends, alongside a handful of academy players (and the odd local ring-in to cover the inevitable injuries). Players were selected for each team via an NFL-style draft. There’s a sliding scale of wages in each team, with two marquee players in every franchise at the top of the payroll. Prize money is on offer to the champions, MVPs and coaches.

Rugby.body:

Both players received red cards in Aix-en-Provence in the first half of the WXV Global Series 2026 fixture. At one stage of the match, France were reduced to 11 players.

Rugby.title: ‘Number one on my goal list’: Sisilia Tuipulotu eyes Lions spot
Rugby.summary: Scoring two tries in a big win is usually a good feeling for a player. Doing that in front of the British & Irish Lions Women coach, Jo Yapp, it is an excellent audition.
Rugby.body:
Scoring two tries in a big win is usually a good feeling for a player. Doing that in front of the British & Irish Lions Women coach, Jo Yapp, it is an excellent audition. That is exactly what Sisilia Tuipulotu did on Friday night as Wales started their WXV Global Series campaign with a 50-19 win against the Springbok Women at Cardiff Arms Park.

“I actually didn’t know she [Yapp] was there until after the game, but I’m very happy that we gave the performance that we did on Friday in front of her,” Tuipulotu said. The spectre of the first-ever Lions Women tour will hang over women’s rugby for the next 12 months and Yapp’s attendance at fixtures will become the subject of plenty speculation about how the team will lineup in New Zealand.

Rugby.body:
Scotland prop Alec Hepburn hopes his summer move to Edinburgh can propel him to the forefront of Gregor Townsend’s plans as a year-long battle to make the 2027 World Cup begins in earnest this weekend.

The Australia-born loosehead previously won six caps for England under Eddie Jones in 2018 amid a productive nine-year stint at Exeter, where he helped the Chiefs to two English titles including a domestic-European double in 2020.

Zebo, 36, who won two URC crowns in 2011 and 2023, believes that strength in depth will be key for Leinster, as will the confidence gained from back-to-back Grand Final victories over the Bulls.

Rugby.title: Stormers make second signing in as many days
Rugby.summary: The Stormers have made their second scrum-half signing in two days, bringing in former Bulls and Lions No.9 Andre Warner on a short-term deal with the new United Rugby Championship season just days away.
Rugby.body:
The Stormers have made their second scrum-half signing in two days, bringing in former Bulls and Lions No.9 Andre Warner on a short-term deal with the new United Rugby Championship season just days away.

Following the signing of former Junior Springboks star Haashim Pead, the Stormers have signed the 33-year-old to bolster their scrum-half stocks, which were looking thin. The club recently confirmed that 22-year-old scrum-half Imad Khan will miss much of the season after injuring his ACL against the All Blacks. With Cobus Reinach also expected to miss a large chunk of the season while with the Springboks, they have now addressed what appeared to be an area of concern.

Rugby.title: Scarlets ready to 'come out fighting' with future at stake
Rugby.summary: Scarlets director of rugby Nigel Davies says talk about the organisation's long-term future has galvanised his squad before the new season starts this weekend.
Rugby.body:
Scarlets director of rugby Nigel Davies says talk about the organisation's long-term future has galvanised his squad before the new season starts this weekend. The Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) has outlined how it plans to cut from four men's professional teams to three by 2028, with Ospreys and Scarlets set to fight to be the side in west Wales.

The governing body says the decision will be made in time for the 2028-29 season, with one side in the capital, one in the east and one in the west. WRU-owned Cardiff and Dragons, an independently backed business, are set to be given licences in the capital and east respectively.

Rugby.title: Pollock left money on table to stay at Saints
Rugby.summary: Henry Pollock turned down rival offers worth much more than his Northampton extension, which will earn him over £400,000 a year, says adviser Eddie Hearn.
Rugby.body:
Henry Pollock turned down rival offers worth hundreds of thousands of pounds more than his extension to stay at boyhood club Northampton, says Eddie Hearn. Hearn, whose Matchroom promotional empire is centred on boxing, darts and snooker, has been working as Pollock's adviser since March.

Pollock, 21, has agreed a new deal with Saints that extends his terms to summer 2028 and is worth more than £400,000 a year. "There were a couple of domestic offers – a couple of Prem offers - and international offers as well," said Hearn of Pollock's options during his renegotiation.

Rugby.title: 'The World Cup left a bad taste': Sara Mannini and Italy ready for Springbok Women rematch
Rugby.summary: Sara Mannini has experienced plenty of changes over the past few months. But happily for her and the rest of the Italy squad, one thing that didn’t change was maintaining their winning ways by defeating Japan in their opening WXV Global Series fixture.
Rugby.body:
Sara Mannini has experienced plenty of changes over the past few months. But happily for her and the rest of the Italy squad, one thing that didn’t change was maintaining their winning ways by defeating Japan in their opening WXV Global Series fixture.

It means Italy have won three of their last four fixtures, with the 55-21 victory added to their wins over Scotland and Wales in the 2026 Guinness Women’s Six Nations. Mannini played the full 80 minutes at Stadio Omero Tognon in Italy’s north-east, and it is an exciting time for the 21-year-old.

Rugby.title: Rassie won’t be fooled again but ‘there may not be better time for Australia to meet Boks’
Rugby.summary: It might not be humiliating, but it would certainly be embarrassing for South Africa to lose to lowly Australia again.
Rugby.body:
So sang Roger Daltry and The Who back in the day, but it could easily have been Rassie Erasmus late last week as he emerged from his mini-break on Australia’s east coast. The Springboks coach spoke to local media as the South Africans confirmed they will play Fiji in Gosford on the NSW Central Coast next September, a final pre-Rugby World Cup hit-out for both sides two weeks before the tournament kicks off.

Both teams will be based on the Central Coast next year and the Boks have used the last fortnight to familiarise themselves with their 2027 RWC training base, while they rest up and recover from the four-Test Greatest Rivalry series against New Zealand.

Rugby.summary: After falling short of the play-offs, which had been the benchmark for the club since Alex Sanderson's arrival in January 2021, the Sharks need to deliver a top-four finish, if not better, this time around.
Rugby.body:
After falling short of the play-offs, which had been the benchmark for the club since Alex Sanderson’s arrival in January 2021, the Sharks need to deliver a top-four finish, if not better, this time around, to justify the investment made in the squad.

The signing of Courtney Lawes from France and Nicky Smith from Leicester were statements of intent by the Sharks owners, while the arrival of England internationals Joe Marchant and Alex Lozowski has added considerable experience to the backline. Sanderson is a man of integrity and knows there can’t be any excuses for failure this time around.

Rugby.title: Max Malins: 'I never really feel I played my best stuff for England and that time may have passed'
Rugby.summary: The Saracens playmaker has a complex history with England, as he explains candidly in a wide-ranging interview.
Rugby.body:
Max Malins didn’t feel nervous. He’d put in the groundwork. Exclusive use of a Majorcaroof terrace had been secured. An overzealous restaurant manager recruited as accomplice. Phone wedged in a plant pot to capture the momentous seconds he’d ask partner Ella to be his wife.

As the couple gazed out across the sunlit hills of the Balearic island, Malins plucked the diamond ring from his pocket and began what’s best described as a torturous descent to the ground. His right leg jolted as if struck by a cattle prod. His knee buckled like a rotten tree trunk. For a beat, it looked like Malins was bound, head over heels, for the concrete. When the video was uploaded to Instagram, the boys back at Saracens had a field day in the comments.

Rugby.title: WXV Global Series 2026: Week 2 talking points
Rugby.summary: Well. That was brilliant. WXV Global Series 2026 is very much living up to expectation. Last weekend proves that beyond doubt.
Rugby.body:
Well. That was brilliant. WXV Global Series 2026 is very much living up to expectations. Last weekend proves that beyond doubt. On the second weekend of Test matches across Europe, we saw England held steady by Canada. Ireland could not stop the USA from registering an upset. Wales started their autumn with a bang against the Springbok Women. France overcame a frustrating first half. The Black Ferns kept their winning streak alive. And Italy picked up an impressive win against the Sakura Fifteen.

Yes, you read that right. England’s 39-game winning streak is over. Ended by a thrilling 26-26 draw with Canada in a repeat of the two teams’ Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 final a year prior.

Rugby.title: Gloucester choose another Welshman as captain for the 2026/27 season
Rugby.summary: Having been led by Tomos Williams last season, Gloucester have handed the captain's armband for the upcoming 2026/27 campaign to fellow Welsh international Dewi Lake.
Rugby.body:
Having been led by Tomos Williams last season, Gloucester have handed the captain’s armband for the upcoming 2026/27 campaign to fellow Welsh international Dewi Lake. Scrum-half Williams’ departure to Saracens left Gloucester needing an alternative captain and they have turned to Lake, who has plenty of leadership experience for both his former club the Ospreys and at international level.

Lake has captained Wales in 22 of his 36 Tests and filled in for the injured Jac Morgan during the Six Nations and the Nations Championship. The 27-year-old will be supported by two vice captains: England centre, Seb Atkinson, and fellow summer signing and old Ospreys teammate, Morgan.

Rugby.title: Exeter boss Rob Baxter gives insight into Henry Slade contract negotiations
Rugby.summary: Slade, 34, who has made 268 appearances for the Chiefs, is one of the last remaining members of the side that won the PREM and Champions Cup double six years ago.
Rugby.body:
Exeter Chiefs boss Rob Baxter says he will sit down in the next month with England outside centre Henry Slade to discuss him taking up the option for a second year in his current deal.

Slade, 34, who has made 268 appearances for the Chiefs, is one of the last remaining members of the side that won the PREM and Champions Cup double six years ago. And Baxter says that there are loads of reasons why Slade, who has won 78 England caps and started his career on a dual-registration at Plymouth Albion 15 years ago, will activate the clause and not finish his career with a lucrative move abroad or join one of their rivals.

Rugby.summary: Springboks coach Rassie Erasmus has made 13 changes to the starting side that defeated the All Blacks in Baltimore earlier this month.
Rugby.body:
Springboks coach Rassie Erasmus has made 13 changes to the starting side that defeated the All Blacks in Baltimore earlier this month, with Andre Esterhuizen set to captain the side for the first time against the Wallabies in Perth.

Erasmus has made mass changes to the side that secured a 3-1 series win in Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry, with Eben Etzebeth and Ethan Hooker retaining their spots in an otherwise new-look run-on side for the one-off Test.

Rugby.summary: The back rower has already amassed a career’s worth of accolades at the age of just 21 – boasting 49 Saints appearances, 13 England caps, a Lions tour and, most recently, a Gallagher PREM winners’ medal.
Rugby.body:
Northampton Saints have confirmed that England star Henry Pollock, one of the game’s most recognisable figures, will remain at his boyhood club after signing a new long-term deal.

The Lions back row joined Saints four years ago as a 17-year-old schoolboy and became the first rugby player to join Eddie Hearn’s Matchroom Talent agency earlier this year. He could celebrate his new deal by making his 50th Saints appearance against Newcastle Red Bulls, who attempted to lure him away from Franklin’s Gardens this weekend.

"I am very, very happy to sign here," Pollock told BBC Radio Northampton. "I have been here my whole career so it made sense for me to stay on the journey with such a young group of players, who are so ambitious.

Rugby.summary: Australia assistant coach Tom Donnelly has likened the intensity of the Springboks to what the Wallabies will experience at Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027.
Rugby.body:
Australia assistant coach Tom Donnelly has likened the intensity of the Springboks to what the Wallabies will experience at Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027, drawing on the level seen during the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Series.

South Africa claimed a 3-1 series win against their opponents from New Zealand, which included a Test played in front of more than 68,000 fans in Baltimore. They have since flown from the United States to the east coast of Australia, and will head to Perth later this week.

Rugby.summary: "No, I agree with Mils. But I don't think you can drop someone out yet. I think Fabian Holland's definite to keep in there. I think he's one of the boys for the future who's doing exceptionally well," Putt said on his first appearance on The Breakdown.
Rugby.body:
With only two weeks to go until the Wallabies travel to New Zealand for the Bledisloe Cup series, former All Blacks captain Scott Barrett is racing the clock to be named in Dave Rennie’s 34-man squad.

Barrett hasn’t featured for the All Blacks since last year’s end-of-year tour, taking nearly a full season off Super Rugby Pacific on a non-playing sabbatical. His return was scheduled before the start of the Super Rugby Pacific playoffs with the Crusaders, but a back injury ruined any chance of pulling on the red-and-black shirt in 2026.

Rugby.body:

Rugby.body:
Wallabies backrower Charlie Cale has sustained a shoulder injury in the lead-up to the clash with the Springboks and is now set to return to Canberra. One-time Australia captain Nick Champion de Crespigny has been called into the squad for the first time under Les Kiss.

Cale has endured a tough run with injuries over recent seasons, having gone two years between appearances in Wallaby gold, before featuring in four Tests this season. But the loose forward has suffered another setback, as the Wallabies confirmed in a squad update on Tuesday.

Rugby.title: Raffi Quirke's Newcastle career gets off to false start after injury setback
Rugby.summary: Newcastle Red Bulls boss Dan McFarland has confirmed that England scrum-half Raffi Quirke has been ruled out of the season opener against reigning Gallagher PREM champions Northampton Saints at Franklin’s Gardens on Friday night.
Rugby.body:
Newcastle Red Bulls boss Dan McFarland has confirmed that England scrum-half Raffi Quirke has been ruled out of the season opener against reigning Gallagher PREM champions Northampton Saints at Franklin’s Gardens on Friday night.

RugbyPass understands that Quirke, who moved from Sale Sharks this summer, has damaged knee ligaments and that the club have started to search for a potential replacement. The news will be a blow to Quirke, who suffered a string of hamstring and wrist injuries during his time with the Sharks and hoped a move to the North East would kick-start his stalled international career.

Ireland international Sean Jansen has extended his stay at Connacht beyond the end of this season after signing a new two-year deal, which will run until at least 2029. The No.8’s current contract was due to expire next summer but the western province have moved quickly to secure the services of last season’s Player of the Year.

Last season he scored 12 tries in 20 appearances, while he also made an immense contribution in defence, coming third in the URC rankings for tackles made (219).

Rugby.summary: Jamie Bhatti's second spell at Bath has been derailed almost as soon as it has begun after the Scotland prop revealed he has broken his arm via social media.
Rugby.body:
Jamie Bhatti’s second spell at Bath has been derailed almost as soon as it has begun after the Scotland prop revealed he has broken his arm via social media. Bhatti posted an image of an x-ray revealing the fracture on his personal Instagram account, which has yet to be officially confirmed by the club.

The 33-year-old, who arrived in the summer on a two-year deal, suffered the injury 10 minutes after coming on against his former club Glasgow in Bath’s final pre-season game at Old Anniesland last Friday.

Pollock, who was offered a deal by Newcastle Red Bulls, has been closing in on a new contract with the Gallagher PREM champions for the last few weeks, despite saying last week in a pre-season media session that he was open to offers.

Rugby.body:
Munster’s squad for 2026/27 feels like one caught between cycles. Clayton McMillan’s outfit remains capable of putting a highly competitive XV on the field, but a closer look at the depth chart reveals a group that is still searching for its next generation of talent and one that is light on marquee players.

There is quality in key areas. Tadhg Beirne remains world-class, Craig Casey is central to almost everything Munster do, and Jack Crowley, if he can get back to full fitness in 2027, is still the standout talent in the backline.

Rugby.title: 'I want people to know who Rodrigo Marta is' - Portugal's history-making Top 14 try machine
Rugby.summary: Once lax and unprofessional, Marta is now approaching half a century of Test tries, including the most famous score in Portuguese rugby history.
Rugby.body:
Rodrigo Marta scores tries. He has scored against Hong Kong China. He has scored against Switzerland. He has scored against most of the nations on the Rugby Europe scene. He has scored twice in one game against the Azzurri of Italy. He has scored a bucketload in the ProD2 in France at a rate of close to one every other match. Recently, Marta has scored five tries in three games at the start of this Top 14 season. And he scored the most famous try in Portuguese rugby history, a swan dive in the south of France which took the Lobos to the promised land.

At just 26 years old, the Section Paloise back has 42 Test tries. On rugby’s all time list of international scorers, he is above Damian Penaud and Adam Ashley-Cooper. Jeff Wilson, Christian Cullen and Brian O’Driscoll are a few ahead of him. Marta is seven tries adrift of a place in the top 10.

World Cup winner Joe Worsley believes reigning champions South Africa have created the template that can take Georgia to the next level as they prepare to face the Springboks in next year’s Rugby World Cup in Australia.

Worsley, who will be part of the Georgia coaching group for a third successive World Cup campaign, played in three tournaments for England, including the 2003 triumph in Australia. Rugby.summary: Shaun Edwards' first coaching role since his shock exit as France's defence coach has been revealed.
Rugby.body:
Shaun Edwards’ first coaching role since his shock exit as France’s defence coach has been revealed. The 59-year-old has joined up with John Mitchell’s Red Roses set-up on a short-term deal ahead of the world champions’ WXV Global Series fixture with the Black Ferns at Allianz Stadium this weekend. He will remain with England until the conclusion of WXV Global Series.

Edwards left his role with Fabien Galthie’s team in the summer after nearly six years in the role. During his time in the role, France enjoyed Guinness Six Nations Grand Slam success in 2022 and back-to-back titles in 2025 and 2026.

Rugby.title: Edwards signs short-term deal with Red Roses
Rugby.summary: Shaun Edwards has started a short-term coaching consultancy role with England women.
Rugby.body:
Shaun Edwards has started a short-term coaching consultancy role with England women. It is understood the 59-year-old will work with current Red Roses defence coach Sarah Hunter for the rest of their WXV Global Series matches, starting with New Zealand at Allianz Stadium on Saturday.

The news comes after England's 39-Test winning streak ended with a 26-26 draw against Canada last weekend. Englishman Edwards is one of the most decorated coaches in rugby union. He recently left his role as France men's defence coach, where he won three Six Nations titles.

Rugby.title: Canada proved against the Red Roses you do not always have to 'earn the right to go wide'
Rugby.summary: Canada's innovative and educated players disproved Warren Gatland's old maxim as they ended England's winning run in a thrilling WXV Global Series draw.
Rugby.body:
The first coach of standing in the professional game who uttered the phrase was Wales head honcho Warren Gatland. “You have to earn the right to go wide,” he claimed in the early years of his tenure. Since then, it has passed into common currency and become the mantra of collision-based footy.

Very few stopped to argue the toss because of the outstanding stream of results in Gatland’s first spell: a Six Nations title at his first tilt in 2008; then five more, including three Grand Slams in the course of his 12-year period in charge. Wales reached the semi-final of the World Cup twice, in 2011 and 2019, and even briefly held the number one ranking in the world.

Rugby.title: ‘We’re still at the beginning’: Italy head coach sets expectations after Japan win
Rugby.summary: Despite a 55-21 win against Japan, Italy head coach Plinio Sciamanna believes his team still have work to do.
Rugby.body:
After a 55-21 win against Japan in his first game as Italy head coach, Plinio Sciamanna believes his team has plenty of room for improvement. The Azzurre combined forward power with attacking flair to put Japan under sustained pressure as they began life under Sciamanna on a positive note.

After tries from Aura Muzzo and Alessandra Frangipani in the middle part of the first half, the Sakura Fifteen responded with converted efforts from Nami Asari and Asuka Kuge to briefly turn the tide.

Rugby.title: Cornish Pirates impress in opening day Doncaster win
Rugby.summary: Cornish Pirates get their Champ season off to an excellent start as they beat Doncaster Knights 45-19 at the Mennaye Field.
Rugby.body:
Cornish Pirates got their Champ season off to an excellent start as they beat Doncaster Knights 45-19 at the Mennaye Field. Replacement hooker Matt Pritchard scored four tries after the interval to add to three first-half scores as the Cornish side were one of three Champ teams to get a bonus-point win in their opening game.

“I’m really pleased," Cornish Pirates joint-head coach Alan Paver told BBC Radio Cornwall. "A full house at the Mennaye, the grass is looking green, the sun's out and you're always a little bit apprehensive first game of the season against a quality side.

Rugby.title: Rachel Malcolm: 'It feels like there’s hope again'
Rugby.summary: Rachel Malcolm insisted Scotland can take positives from their 66-14 defeat against the Black Ferns.
Rugby.body:
Rachel Malcolm insisted Scotland can take positives from their 66-14 defeat against the Black Ferns. Whitney Hansen’s New Zealand scored 10 tries at Hive Stadium to win their first-ever fixture in the Scottish capital. Scotland’s points came thanks to a pair of Evie Gallagher tries that were both converted by Helen Nelson.

The hosts have now conceded 130 points in their two WXV Global Series matches this autumn and will welcome the Wallaroos to Edinburgh next weekend. It will be the first of three Tests between the two teams over the next four weeks.

Rugby.summary: The Springboks arrive in Perth without Pieter-Steph du Toit and Damian de Allende after the veteran duo were released from the squad to spend more time with family.
Rugby.body:
This is how Wallabies flanker Carlo Tizzano wants this weekend to pan out: Fremantle saluting in the AFL grand final on Saturday and Australia beating world champions South Africa in front of a rocking Optus Stadium crowd on Sunday night.

Perth is abuzz with Flagmantle fever ahead of the Dockers’ date with destiny against Brisbane at the MCG on Saturday. It’s little wonder the Wallabies’ arrival in Perth has gone mostly unnoticed.

Rugby.title: The three big takeaways from round two of Super Rugby Australia
Rugby.summary: Despite the results blowing out at the weekend, the Super Rugby AUS competition is definitely fulfilling its purpose.
Rugby.body:
Super Rugby AUS Round 2 has come and gone, and it delivered great running rugby, big hits, tactical and skillful play, as well as two thrashings. Overall, the NSW Waratahs are the biggest dog in the yard at the moment, with the Western Force not far behind in their ability to lure their opponents into a scrappy dog fight whilst finishing them off with flair on the edges.

The ACT Brumbies’ Super Rugby Pacific backline is grossly underperforming and is not being helped by their beaten pack. Their scrum is their clear shining light. The Queensland Reds continue to struggle with a flat attack and appear unable to get any sort of foothold of momentum in their games.

Rugby.title: Tiatia in talks over new Dragons deal
Rugby.summary: Dragons aim to secure new contract with head coach Filo Tiatia as he prepares for a second full season in charge at Rodney Parade.
Rugby.body:
Dragons are in advanced talks with head coach Filo Tiatia about a contract extension. The former All Blacks forward joined the Rodney Parade club in the summer of 2024 as defence coach.

He was promoted as interim boss after the departure of Dai Flanagan the following November and was appointed on a permanent basis in February 2025. Tiatia's deal expires at the end of the 2026-27 campaign and Dragons are keen to retain his services.

Rugby.title: California Legion appoint former Fijian Drua boss as new head coach
Rugby.summary: “I’m incredibly excited to be joining California Legion and to have the opportunity to lead the club into the 2027 season," Jackson said.
Rugby.body:
Former international referee Glen Jackson has been appointed as the new head coach of California Legion, ahead of the 2027 Major League Rugby campaign. Legion, who finished runners-up in the 2026 season, will have Jackson’s wide range of experience to call upon in 2027, after a career as a player, referee, and head coach.

Jackson heads to California after beginning his coaching career under current Queensland Reds head coach Vern Cotter with Fiji, before transitioning into the Fijian Drua head coaching role.

Rugby.title: ‘The belief was there’: Hanratty hails USA’s remarkable Ireland comeback
Rugby.summary: After his USA Women’s Eagles side overturned a 19-point deficit to beat Ireland 40-36 in their WXV Global Series opener, Skerries-born head coach Jack Hanratty hailed his young team's resilience.
Rugby.body:
After his USA Women’s Eagles side overturned a 19-point deficit to beat Ireland 40-36 in their WXV Global Series opener, Skerries-born head coach Jack Hanratty hailed his young team’s resilience.

For much of the first half at Tallaght Stadium the North Americans struggled to impose themselves. Ireland made the most of that and scored four tries in the opening 30 minutes. Tries from the USA’s Georgie Perris-Redding and Hope Rogers meant the half-time scoreboard read 24-12 in favour of the hosts.

Rugby.title: Erin King has ‘no doubt’ about Ireland after shock loss
Rugby.summary: Four tries up at half-time, a dominant display from both the forwards and backs putting in powerful displays, and a green wave of support behind them at Tallaght Stadium in Dublin. Ireland looked firmly in control in their WXV Global Series opener.
Rugby.body:
Four tries up at half-time, Ireland looked firmly in control of their WXV Global Series opener at Tallaght Stadium in Dublin, with dominant displays from both the forwards and backs and a green wave of support behind them.

Yet, 40 minutes later, the home side were left stunned as the USA Women’s Eagles produced a huge second-half comeback to snatch a 40-36 victory and start their campaign strongly.

Rugby.title: 'I learned nothing': France coach Ratier unimpressed despite dramatic Wallaroos comeback
Rugby.summary: France head coach François Ratier claimed he learned nothing new about his team after they completed an unlikely comeback to beat the Wallaroos.
Rugby.body:
France head coach François Ratier claimed he learned nothing new about his team after they completed an unlikely comeback to beat the Wallaroos. In Aix-en-Provence, Ratier watched his team score 17 unanswered points in the second half to overcome Australia to win 29-26.

It is a result made all the more impressive when you consider that, at one stage in the first half, France were reduced to 11 players on the pitch. A wild seven minutes saw Ambre Mwayembe receive a 20-minute red card, while both Lea Champon and Léa Murie received yellow cards for high tackles and Cloe Correa received a straight red card for eye-gouging in a maul.

Rugby.title: Eagles switch attention to Wales after ‘setting the tone’ with Ireland win
Rugby.summary: The USA Women’s Eagles kicked off their WXV Global Series campaign with a statement 40-36 victory over Ireland at Tallaght Stadium in Dublin.
Rugby.body:
The USA Women’s Eagles kicked off their WXV Global Series campaign with a statement 40-36 victory over Ireland at Tallaght Stadium in Dublin. It was a pulsating 80 minutes of rugby, with Ireland taking a 24-12 lead into the break before the USA produced a remarkable second-half comeback. Four tries after the interval turned the game on its head and saw the Eagles hold their nerve to claim a memorable victory on Irish soil.

Kathryn Treder crossed twice in the second half, with Hallie Taufoou and player of the match Freda Tafuna also finding the try line as Jack Hanratty’s side secured a thrilling win that will provide plenty of confidence heading into the remainder of their WXV Global Series campaign.

Rugby.title: USA loss a game Ireland 'should have won'
Rugby.summary: Ireland head coach Scott Bemand says their defeat against USA in the WXV Global Series opener at Tallaght Stadium was "a game we should have won".
Rugby.body:
Ireland head coach Scott Bemand said their defeat against USA in the WXV Global Series opener at Tallaght Stadium was "a game we should have won". USA, led by County Dublin-born head coach Jack Hanratty, fought back from trailing 31-12 at one stage of the second half to score four successive tries and claim a 40-36 comeback win.

A loss of discipline in the second half contributed to Ireland's loss after their impressive first-half display, and Bemand was frustrated that they let the game slip out of their control.

Rugby.title: URC 2026/2027 squads rated: Leinster
Rugby.summary: Leinster head into 2026/27 in a slightly unusual position. For all the familiar talk of depth, production lines and international quality, this is a squad that feels...
Rugby.body:
Leinster head into 2026/27 in a slightly unusual position. For all the familiar talk of depth, production lines and international quality, this is a squad that feels a little less bombproof than in recent years. There is still exceptional strength in key areas, particularly at hooker, lock and back row, where Leo Cullen can call upon a wealth of proven Test talent.

But there are also genuine questions to answer across the front row, in midfield and out wide. The departures of James Lowe, Rieko Ioane, Ciarán Frawley and Luke McGrath have stripped away experience and versatility, while Rabah Slimani’s exit leaves renewed scrutiny on a tighthead position that has been a long-running concern.
