Rugby.title: Ireland player ratings v USA | WXV Global Series 2026
Rugby.summary: Tallaght Stadium was stunned into relative silence as the USA Women's Eagles secured a 40-36 win over Ireland in Dublin to start their WXV Global Series campaign.
Rugby.body:
Tallaght Stadium was stunned into relative silence as the USA Women’s Eagles secured a 40-36 win over Ireland in Dublin to start their WXV Global Series campaign. Jack Hanratty’s side led by 12 points at half-time, with tries from Vicky Elmes Kinlan, Cliodhna Moloney-MacDonald, Aoife Wafer and Eve Higgins putting the hosts in control.

But the USA hit back after the break, with Kathryn Treder scoring twice before Hallie Taufoou and Freda Tafuna also crossed to complete a stunning comeback. Provided the assist for Vicky Elmes Kinlan’s try in the sixth minute. The full-back contributed plenty to her team in attack, but did turn the ball over on a couple of occasions and gave the USA good field position from which to mount attacks.

Rugby.title: USA stun Ireland with comeback WXV win in Dublin
Rugby.summary: The United States stage a remarkable second-half comeback to beat Ireland 40-36 in their WXV Global Series opener at Tallaght Stadium.
Rugby.body:
The United States staged a remarkable second-half comeback to beat Ireland 40-36 in their WXV Global Series opener at Tallaght Stadium. Scott Bemand's side raced into a comfortable lead after 20 minutes following tries from Vicky Elmes Kinlan, Cliodhna Moloney-MacDonald and Aoife Wafer and went in 24-12 ahead at the break.

Erin King added a fifth try early in the second half as Ireland looked to be cruising at 31-12 up, but a loss of control and discipline aided USA, who under the guidance of their Irish head coach Jack Hanratty, managed to turn the game around.

Rugby.title: Welsh rugby's key signings ahead of new season
Rugby.summary: Four summer signings are tipped to make a big impact at Cardiff, Dragons, Ospreys and Scarlets in the 2026-27 United Rugby Championship.
Rugby.body:
Wales' regions may have seen more star names depart but the summer has also seen one of the most active recruitment drives in recent years. There were notable departures with the loss of Jac Morgan, Dewi Lake, Aaron Wainwright and Marnus van der Merwe.

And Welsh professional men's rugby continues to be hit by off-field uncertainty with the WRU committed to cutting the number of regions from four to three. But Cardiff, Dragons, Ospreys and Scarlets - now all signed up to the new participation agreement and an increase in annual budget - have made significant additions as they seek old heads and overseas talent to help develop young homegrown squads for the 2026-27 season.

Rugby.title: Waisea Nayacalevu makes drastic position switch on debut for new club
Rugby.summary: Former Fiji captain Waisea Nayacalevu will make his debut for Rugby Olympique de Grasse, but in an unusual role: at no.8 for the Fédérale 2 club.
Rugby.body:
Former Fiji captain Waisea Nayacalevu will make his debut for Rugby Olympique de Grasse, but in an unusual role: at no.8 for the Fédérale 2 club. Nayacalevu left Nissa Rugby after helping the club secure promotion to the Pro D2, scoring three tries in 11 appearances for the southeastern French side. However, when his centre contract wasn’t renewed, he was free to find a new club, and RO Grasse stepped in, signing the Fijian legend for an undisclosed number of seasons.

Fédérale 2 is the fifth tier of French club rugby, sitting below the Top 14, Pro D2, Nationale and Fédérale 1, and is a predominantly amateur competition, although some clubs also field semi-professional players.

Rugby.title: Fergus Watson: 'I grew up wearing my granddad's Scotland cap
Rugby.summary: The muscular Glasgow back took seamlessly to men's rugby and longs to follow in his grandfather's footsteps by playing for Scotland.
Rugby.body:
As a young boy in Biggar, Fergus Watson coveted his grandfather’s Scotland cap. Bill Watson is in his late seventies now but some 50 years ago, wore the thistle 10 times alongside such giants as Andy Irvine, Ian McLauchlan, Jim Renwick and Sir Ian McGeechan. He would later run the whole Scottish Rugby enterprise as CEO during the turbulent early years of professionalism.

More than two decades since leaving office, those connections are still felt by his 21-year-old grandson, a muscle-bound wing who should see meaningful action for Glasgow this season. Usually, the familial memories are warm. Sometimes, though, the ripples from the past hit different.

Rugby.title: Munster relying on youth and a discarded talent as fly-half crisis comes to a head
Rugby.summary: Besieged by injuries in the number 10 position, the Irish province are growing increasingly desperate as the new season looms.
Rugby.body:
Eighteen months ago, Charlie O’Shea climbed the steps of the main stand at Virgin Media Park in Cork to lift the Munster Schools Senior Cup. His proud mother, Hilary, had the honour of presenting him with the Garrett Fitzgerald Trophy as hundreds of Christian Brothers College students roared their approval. It was a fitting end to O’Shea’s senior cup cycle. He was CBC’s primary fly-half through fourth, fifth and sixth year, but lost 2023 and 2024 finals to local rivals, Presentation Brothers College. He would leave CBC as a Schools Cup-winning captain.

On Friday, O’Shea shone on his first start with Munster’s senior team against two-time Champions Cup winners Leicester Tigers, at the same venue where he hoisted the silverware aloft. The 20-year-old grew up playing for Dolphin and had 15 All-Ireland League appearances for University College Cork last season. He is the last fly-half standing between Munster’s senior and academy squads. The United Rugby Championship season has not even begun.

Rugby.title: All Blacks ‘need to get rid of ill-discipline and rediscover lost art of building pressure’
Rugby.summary: New Zealand used to squeeze teams into submission with 'weaponised excellence', in the same way the Springboks have just done to them.
Rugby.body:
After four Tests against a Springboks team that is becoming one of the all-time greats, the All Blacks have learned that their single biggest failing is they have lost the art of building pressure.

When they were the game’s leading team and chasing greatness between 2010 and 2019 the way South Africa now are, the All Blacks knew how to build and maintain pressure on their opposition by stacking repeat moments of calm, accurate and disciplined play.

Rugby.body:

Canada had won just three of the last 16 meetings between the North American sides, as they looked ahead to the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup third-place playoff. They were looking to back up their heroics from last year, having claimed a 14-point win over the Eagles in Calgary.

Scotland suffered a second successive defeat in the WXV Global Series as New Zealand ran out comfortable winners at Hive Stadium. The Black Ferns ran in 10 tries while the Scots struggled to contain the number two ranked team in the world.

New Zealand took no time at all to exert their dominance, punching holes in the Scottish defence before powerful prop Mo'omo'oga Palu blasted through to score. The Black Ferns set a tempo the Scots could just not live with, and another foray into the Scottish 22 resulted in a neat finish from lock Maama Mo'onia Vaipulu for the second try.

Rugby.title: The Red Roses four-year winning streak ends on 39 games with Canada draw
Rugby.summary: England’s four-year winning run came to an end as they were held to a 26-26 draw by a Canada side they beat in last year’s Women's Rugby World Cup final.
Rugby.body:
England’s four-year winning run came to an end as they were held to a 26-26 draw by a Canada side they beat in last year’s Women’s Rugby World Cup final. A thrilling eight-try game was level at the hour mark after Olivia Apps crossed for Canada in what turned out to be the final score of the contest.

England pushed for their 40th straight win in the closing stages but were held at bay by determined defending from the visitors at Exeter’s Sandy Park. New Zealand remain the last team to have beaten the Red Roses, in the 2022 Rugby World Cup final.

Rugby.title: 'We wanted to go for the win': Why Canada took a draw against the Red Roses
Rugby.summary: When Claire Gallagher booted the ball into touch at full-time of Canada's 26-26 draw with the Red Roses, there were boos at Sandy Park.
Rugby.body:
When Claire Gallagher booted the ball into touch at full-time of Canada’s 26-26 draw with the Red Roses, there were boos at Sandy Park. The sold-out crowd in Devon wanted to see a winner. Everyone across the world did. Even so, you could see the practicality in the world’s third-ranked side taking a first-ever draw against the team that bested them in the Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 final.

It had been an enthralling WXV Global Series encounter between the two teams. From start to finish, they went blow for blow. Thankfully, we will get two more instalments of these foes battling it out in October in Toronto and Ottawa.

Rugby.title: Canada end England's 39-game winning run with frenetic draw
Rugby.summary: England's remarkable winning run comes to an end as they are held to a nail-biting 26-26 draw by Canada at Sandy Park.
Rugby.body:
England's remarkable 39-match winning run came to an end as they were held to a nail-biting 26-26 draw by Canada at Sandy Park. The Red Roses were unable to escape the clutches of a relentless Canada, who they beat in last year's World Cup final, with the two sides sharing four tries apiece in front of a raucous 14,573 crowd in Exeter.

Canada are the first team to avoid defeat against England since New Zealand beat them in the 2022 World Cup final, but John Mitchell's side are now unbeaten in 40 Tests. The draw also ended England's 100% home record against Canada, having won each of their previous 13 home meetings.

Rugby.summary: Canada have beaten the USA Eagles 19-16 in an all-time classic, wrapping up third place at the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup 2026.
Rugby.body:
Canada have beaten the USA Eagles 19-16 in an all-time classic, wrapping up third place at the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup 2026. It was a nail-biter that came right down to the wire, but the Canadians did enough to claim their second consecutive win over their arch-rivals.

The Canadians set the tone early with some physical carries and high-tempo play, and looked to build on the foundations they had set. Canada were almost immediately rewarded for their strong start, with the USA conceding a penalty inside two minutes.

Rugby.title: Wales deliver performance of serious promise
Rugby.summary: Wales have set themselves a new standard after clocking up a half-century of points in their WXV opener against South Africa.
Rugby.body:
Wales have set themselves a new standard after an impressive eight-try victory over South Africa in their WXV Global Series opener. It was a score even the most optimistic of fans could not have predicted against a team who went into the match ranked 10th in the world, three places above Wales, but the 50-19 scoreboard shone bright under Cardiff's Friday night lights.

Sean Lynn's side have been dealt their share of criticism in recent years, and understandably so with a winless World Cup and three Six Nations wooden spoons. But they were unrecognisable in the Welsh capital as players shook off the shackles of the past and delivered a performance of real promise.

Rugby.title: Flying Fijians make late change with Drua winger ruled out of PNC Final
Rugby.summary: Two-time Super Rugby winner Seta Tamanivalu has been brought into the Flying Fijians matchday 23.
Rugby.body:
TOKYO: Two-time Super Rugby winner Seta Tamanivalu has been brought into the Flying Fijians matchday 23 for the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup Final, with winger Manasa Mataele ruled out just before the match in Tokyo.

Tamanivalu joined the squad in Japan this week, with midfielder Kalaveti Ravouvou ruled out of the decider with an injury. 34-year-old Tamanivalu, who used to play for the All Blacks, is now set to represent Fiji for the first time since the 2025 PNC.

Rugby.title: The incredible connection in Flying Fijians side for PNC Final
Rugby.summary: 18 of the 23 Flying Fijians selected for the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup Final currently play club rugby for the Fijian Drua.
Rugby.body:
TOKYO: 18 of the 23 Flying Fijians selected for the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup Final currently play club rugby for the Fijian Drua. Incredibly, some of the club’s all-time greats are among the five others named to take on Japan at Prince Chichibu Memorial Stadium.

Fiji captain Tevita Ikanivere will lead the national team into another Pacific Nations Cup decider, as they look to secure a three-peat. Ikanivere is no longer part of the Fijian Drua squad, having moved to Japan Rugby League One outfit Mie Honda Heat.

Rugby.title: ‘Absolute priority’: Japan eye PNC glory in another final against Fiji
Rugby.summary: Assistant coach Neil Hatley sees winning the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup 2026 Final in Tokyo as an “absolute priority."
Rugby.body:
TOKYO: Assistant coach Neil Hatley sees winning the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup 2026 Final in Tokyo as an “absolute priority” for Japan, who will look to end Fiji’s reign as champions when the two teams meet in another decider on Saturday evening.

Fiji are chasing a third Pacific Nations Cup crown in a row, having claimed silverware when the finals were last held in Japan two years ago. They then repeated that success, taking out the title in Utah last year with a six-point win over Japan.

Rugby.summary: Former NFL draftee Cassh Maluia will debut for the USA Eagles in the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup third-place playoff.
Rugby.body:
TOKYO: Former NFL draftee Cassh Maluia will debut for the USA Eagles in the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup third-place playoff, after being named to start at inside centre in the latest chapter of the USA-Canada sporting rivalry.

Maluia was taken in the sixth round of the 2020 NFL Draft by the New England Patriots, but later made the move to rugby union. The midfielder helped the California Legion reach the 2026 MLR championship game, where they lost to the Chicago Hounds.

Rugby.title: 'I want people to watch what this team is about': Sean Lynn's rallying cry as Wales end wait for win
Rugby.summary: Sean Lynn afforded himself a pleased look at full-time after Wales' 50-19 victory over the Springbok Women.
Rugby.body:
Sean Lynn afforded himself a pleased look at full-time after Wales’ 50-19 victory over the Springbok Women. He took on the role of Wales head coach after guiding Gloucester Hartpury to Premiership Women’s Rugby dominance. The side claimed three league titles in as many years.

Since he first led Wales in the 2025 Guinness Women’s Six Nations, Lynn had only seen his team experience victory once in the 15 Test matches he had presided over. During this time, his team have received back-to-back wooden spoons in the Women’s Six Nations and were dumped out of Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 at the group stage, where they finished with defeat to Fiji.

Rugby.title: Inspired Wales seal stunning win over South Africa
Rugby.summary: Wales return to winning ways in emphatic fashion with an eight-try victory over South Africa at Cardiff Arms Park.
Rugby.body:
Wales returned to winning ways in emphatic fashion with an eight-try victory over South Africa at Cardiff Arms Park. The hosts had gone nine Tests without a victory heading into their WXV Global Series opener, with a tight contest predicted against a Springboks side ranked three places above them in the world.

But Sean Lynn's bold selections paid off as Wales attacked with a freedom and intent they have not produced for years. They were six tries to the good in a dominant first half, with the visitors made to pay for indiscipline.

Rugby.title: Talking points: Wales end 14 months of Test frustration with superb Springboks victory
Rugby.summary: Wales ended a 14-month wait for a Test victory as they opened their WXV Global Series campaign with a convincing 50-19 win over South Africa at Cardiff Arms Park.
Rugby.body:
Wales ended a 14-month wait for a Test victory as they opened their WXV Global Series campaign with a convincing 50-19 win over South Africa at Cardiff Arms Park. Their last win came in July 2025, when Wales beat Australia 21-12 in Ballymore. It is Sean Lynn’s second win as head coach of the team in his 16th Test match at the helm.

By the break, the hosts had crossed the whitewash six times. The scoring started just six minutes in when Courtney Keight crossed the whitewash. The centre was sent over by a combination of a floated Keira Bevan pass and Lisa Neumann sending the Sale Sharks back across.

Rugby.title: URC Champions Leinster name travelling squad for Rainbow Nation tour
Rugby.summary: Three uncapped players and two new signings have made the 41-man squad that heads to South Africa for the first two games of Leinster's URC title defence, against the Lions and Sharks.
Rugby.body:
Leinster have included the majority of their Ireland internationals in the 41-man squad that will head to South Africa for the opening two rounds of the BKT United Rugby Championship.

Jack Conan is the most-capped Leinster player in the group with 180 appearances for the province, and the No.8 is joined by the likes of back-row colleagues Josh van Flier and Jack McCarthy, props Andrew Porter and Tadhg Furlong, hookers Dan Sheehan and Ronan Kelleher, lock James Ryan, fly-half San Prendergast, centres Robbie Henshaw and Garry Ringrose and back-three trio Hugo Keenan and Jimmy and Tommy O’Brien.

Rugby.title: Canada keen to develop 'important relationship' with PWR clubs
Rugby.summary: Canada head coach Kévin Rouet has revealed his ambition to strengthen links between the national team and Premiership Women's Rugby clubs.
Rugby.body:
Canada head coach Kévin Rouet has revealed his ambition to strengthen links between the national team and Premiership Women’s Rugby clubs. Ahead of Canada’s WXV Global Series-opening win against Scotland in Edinburgh, the squad were joined by Trailfinders Women coach Barney Maddison in camp.

The 37-year-old – who coached the West London club to the PWR final last season – joined the squad as a guest coach ahead of Canada’s 64-26 win at Hive Stadium. Rouet already has Saracens director of women’s rugby Alex Austerberry and Loughborough Lightning head coach Nathan Smith as part of his Canada coaching set-up.

Rugby.title: 2026 WXV Global Series preview: Ireland
Rugby.summary: Largely as expected, Ireland were dominant at times against Italy, Wales and Scotland during the 2026 Guinness Women's Six Nations.
Rugby.body:
Largely as expected, Ireland were dominant at times against Italy, Wales and Scotland during the 2026 Guinness Women’s Six Nations. They threw enough punches when losing to France and England to suggest that they are on a path that may well lead to being properly competitive against those nations in the years to come.

The Scotland game was a fantastic way for Ireland to end their Women’s Six Nations campaign, playing arguably the best attacking rugby of the Scott Bemand era in front of a record crowd at the Aviva Stadium.

Rugby.title: Rugby's Greatest Rivalry finale lays foundation for new era for rugby in America before RWC
Rugby.summary: Five years out from RWC 2031, the final Test between New Zealand and South Africa helped win hearts and minds among the US audience.
Rugby.body:
“The USA is at the heart of World Rugby’s new strategic plan.” Word from World Rugby Chair Brett Robinson, who briefed a small group of journalists gathered in the Trust lounge at the Baltimore Ravens M&T Bank Stadium, ahead of the final Test match in Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series.

“Our ambition for 2031,” Robinson continued, “is to ensure that the Rugby World Cup here in the US is the best we’ve ever delivered. Because it’s so important for our game to grow and fuel the sport.”

Rugby.title: Every single World Rugby rankings permutations that can happen this weekend
Rugby.summary: Kévin Rouet's Canada can reclaim second in the World Rugby rankings if they end England's 39-match winning run in Exeter.
Rugby.body:
Kévin Rouet’s Canada can reclaim second in the World Rugby rankings if they end England’s 39-match winning run in Exeter. The second weekend of WXV Global Series action sees a repeat of the Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 final take place at Sandy Park. The North Americans will retake second from the Black Ferns, who would also have to lose to Scotland in this scenario.

John Mitchell’s England can improve their rating for the first time this year with a victory of 15 points or more against Canada. A win by that margin will see the world champions improve by a maximum of 0.25. It will be the highest any England team has ever been rated should their overall rating reach 98.34.

Rugby.title: Finn Russell returns for Bath in final pre-season friendly
Rugby.summary: Scotland and Lions star Finn Russell has been named as Bath's starting fly-half in their final pre-season friendly against his former club Glasgow Warriors at Old Anniesland tonight (Friday).
Rugby.body:
Scotland and Lions star Finn Russell has been named as Bath’s starting fly-half in their final pre-season friendly against his former club Glasgow Warriors at Old Anniesland tonight (Friday).

Russell has been rested up until now, missing the friendly games against Perpignan and Bedford Blues and the PREM Rugby Cup defeat to Sale Sharks. But Bath have brought him back in to pull the strings at 10 against URC powerhouses Glasgow, with the start of the Gallagher PREM season only a week away.

Rugby.title: Rachel Cullum helps Canada to FISU Rugby Sevens Championship
Rugby.summary: Rachel Cullum helps Canada to FISU Rugby Sevens Championship The Queen's Journal
Rugby.body:
Another Gael has shone on the international rugby stage. From Sept. 4 to Sept. 6, Rachel Cullum, ArtSci ’27, helped Canada win the International University Sports Federation (FISU) Women’s Rugby Sevens Championship in South Africa. FISU is an organization in which national teams comprised of all the top university athletes compete against each other.

The Journal sat down with Cullum to talk about winning the championship, as well as her time in South Africa. The team arrived a week early in South Africa to train at the Stellenbosch Academy of Sport training facility, which Cullum believes allowed the team to “connect as a group” and gain an advantage over the other teams who “flew right into the competition.”

Rugby.title: Saints better prepared for Prem title defence
Rugby.summary: Northampton director of rugby Phil Dowson tells the BBC's Saints Show that the club has better chance of defending their title.
Rugby.body:
Northampton Saints are better prepared for this season's defence of their Prem Rugby title than the last time they were champions, according to director of rugby Phil Dowson. Saints finished top of the table in 2025-2026, winning 14 of their 18 matches before beating Exeter 26-17 at Allianz Stadium to lift the trophy in June.

They had also won the title in 2024, but saw a host of top players leave the club including Courtney Lawes, Alex Waller, Lewis Ludlam and Alex Moon before finishing a lowly eighth the following season.

Rugby.title: Adams Verling handed Ireland debut for WXV opener
Rugby.summary: Connacht back row Jemima Adams Verling is handed her senior Ireland debut in Sunday's WXV Global Series opener against the United States in Dublin.
Rugby.body:
Connacht back row Jemima Adams Verling will make her senior Ireland debut in Sunday's WXV Global Series opener against the United States in Dublin. Adams Verling will line out at blind-side flanker in the back row alongside captain Erin King at open-side flanker and Women's Six Nations player of the championship Aoife Wafer at number eight.

The 20-year-old's ascension to the senior team comes after she impressed in the U18 Women's Six Nations in 2024 and last year's U21 Women's Six Nations while she has also been impressive for the Clovers in the Celtic Challenge.

Rugby.summary: Jemima Adams Verling will make her Test debut in Ireland's first WXV Global Series 2026 fixture of the autumn.
Rugby.body:
Jemima Adams Verling will make her Test debut in Ireland’s first WXV Global Series 2026 fixture of the autumn. The Connacht forward will start alongside Ireland captain Erin King and two-time Guinness Women’s Six Nations Player of the Championship, Aoife Wafer, in the back-row.

The 20-year-old is the only uncapped player included in Scott Bemand’s match day squad for Sunday’s match at Dublin’s Tallaght Stadium. Adams Verling has progressed through Ireland’s age-grade ranks and impressed for both the Clovers in Celtic Challenge competition and Connacht in the Vodafone Women’s Interprovincial Championship. She has previously been named in extended Ireland squads.

Rugby.summary: Italy go into the WXV Global Series in a state of flux. They have a new coach, new players have been blooded and while the side has risen through the rankings, many of the same problems remain.
Rugby.body:
Italy go into the WXV Global Series in a state of flux. They have a new coach, new players have been blooded and while the side has risen through the rankings, many of the same problems remain.

Rugby.title: Canada captain still loses sleep over final loss to England
Rugby.summary: Canada captain Sophie de Goede says she still loses sleep over their World Cup final loss to England last year.
Rugby.body:
It is nearly a year since Canada lost the Women's Rugby World Cup final to England - but time has not been a healer for everyone. "Four to five nights a week I can't fall asleep because I'm still thinking about the final," says Canada captain Sophie de Goede, who is preparing to take on the world champions this Saturday at Sandy Park in Exeter.

So, is this match revenge for the side ranked third in the world? Canada head coach Kevin Rouet is keen to play this down: "Revenge is a good brand but they [England] won the final of the World Cup - that was the most important game to win, the next important games will be in the World Cup 2029."

Rugby.title: Ban confirmed: Canada prop learns fate after Scotland red card
Rugby.summary: Canada prop Brittany Kassil has been banned for three matches after her red card against Scotland in her team's WXV Global Series opener.
Rugby.body:
Canada prop Brittany Kassil has been banned for three matches after her red card against Scotland in her team’s WXV Global Series opener. The ban will be reduced to two matches upon the successful completion of World Rugby’s Coaching Intervention Programme.

As things stand, the 35-year-old loosehead prop will miss this weekend’s replay of the Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 final against England, next week’s clash with France in La Rochelle and her team’s first home Test of October, against England at Toronto’s BMO Field.

Rugby.title: Ex-Wales scrum-half Lloyd Williams does retirement u-turn
Rugby.summary: The 36-year-old, who won 32 caps for Wales, made the decision to hang up his boots ahead of last season's play-offs.
Rugby.body:
Former Wales scrum-half Lloyd Williams has decided to sign a new deal with Worcester four months after announcing his retirement from the game. The 36-year-old, who won 32 caps for Wales, made the decision to hang up his boots ahead of last season’s play-offs, which ended with the Warriors winning the Champ in their first season back in professional rugby.

However, Williams has decided he still has some more rugby in him and is now available for selection for tomorrow’s game against Bedford Blues, a re-run of last year’s final. “It’s been a bit of a surreal week, but it’s been great coming back, seeing everyone and fitting back into the environment – everyone’s made me feel really welcome,” said Williams.

However, Williams has decided he still has some more rugby in him and is now available for selection for tomorrow’s game against Bedford Blues, a re-run of last year’s final. “It’s been a bit of a surreal week, but it’s been great coming back, seeing everyone and fitting back into the environment – everyone’s made me feel really welcome,” said Williams.

Rugby.title: 'Unlucky' Ireland second row to miss entirety of WXV Global Series
Rugby.summary: Former Ireland co-captain Sam Monaghan has been ruled out of the team's entire WXV Global Series campaign with an Achilles injury.
Rugby.body:
Former Ireland co-captain Sam Monaghan has been ruled out of the team’s entire WXV Global Series campaign with an Achilles injury. It means that the 33-year-old will miss home Test matches against the USA Women’s Eagles, Japan and tour fixtures against the Springbok Women in Cape Town.

Last year the second row returned from an ACL injury to feature at Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025. She will remain in camp to lend her experience to the group. “Sam has been really unlucky,” Scott Bemand, Ireland head coach, said. “She picked up an Achilles injury, so that will be this competition out for her.

Rugby.summary: The club says there has not been enough demand for the project.
Rugby.body:
A plan for a memorial wall that would have included the ashes of Northampton Saints rugby fans has been cancelled. The Saints Memorial Wall was to have been part of a wider development to enhance the fan village at the Prem Rugby side's Franklin's Gardens ground.

However, the club said initial demand "was not sufficient to support the long-term viability of the development". Supporters who have already paid will receive a refund, Saints said.

Rugby.title: URC trial adds new twist to hotly-debated Rugby's Greatest Rivalry tactic
Rugby.summary: The United Rugby Championship (URC) has decided to bring forward the deadline for team announcements in the upcoming 2026/27 season to 2pm on Thursday.
Rugby.body:
The United Rugby Championship (URC) has decided to bring forward the deadline for team announcements in the upcoming 2026/27 season to 14:00pm (UK time) on Thursday. “Rather than Friday and Saturday teams being announced on separate days, all 16 teams will now work to a coordinated Thursday announcement time. For Friday fixtures, the timing remains largely unchanged, while teams playing on Saturdays and Sundays will generally be announced around 48 hours before kick-off rather than 24 hours,” the URC said in a statement.

Previously, this might have seen as a minor, inconsequential change, but the protocol around team announcements was hotly debated during the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Series (RGRS) between South Africa and New Zealand.

Rugby.title: Exeter Chiefs and Bournemouth share expertise after takeover
Rugby.summary: Exeter boss Rob Baxter says the Prem club has been sharing knowledge with Premier League side AFC Bournemouth.
Rugby.body:
Exeter boss Rob Baxter has said the Prem club has been sharing knowledge with Premier League side AFC Bournemouth. The Chiefs were taken over by the Black Knight group, which also owns the Cherries, at the end of June, becoming the first US-based group to take control of an English Prem rugby side.

Exeter's heads of departments such as strength and conditioning, physiotherapy and sports psychology have since linked up with their peers at Bournemouth. Baxter hopes he and his coaching team can get together with Cherries boss Marco Rose and his backroom team soon.

Rugby.title: Fijiana keen to keep impressing after historic WXV Global Series Challenger victory
Rugby.summary: When match official Amber Stamp-Dunstan whistled for the final time in the Spain-Fiji clash, the Fijiana had made history by beating Las Leonas for the first time.
Rugby.body:
When match official Amber Stamp-Dunstan whistled for the final time in the Spain-Fiji clash, the Fijiana had made history by beating Las Leonas for the first time. The 38-32 win came dramatically, as the Pacific Islanders trailed for most of the game before pulling off a remarkable comeback in the final 13 minutes with tries from Rokowati Nabura, Salote Nailolo and Repeka Adi Tove.

Harlequins’ Manuqalo Komaitai, who came in when the team needed it most, was still elated by what they had pulled off against a formidable Spanish side. “It feels good, as we made history for our country by beating Spain for the first time! I am so proud of the team and the girls for putting in the work and the fight to get this result.”

Rugby.summary: Former Scotland scrum-half Mike Blair reveals his excitement after teaming up with Dave Rennie as New Zealand attack coach and the prospect of facing up against his home country.
Rugby.body:
Foreign coaches are about as rare in All Black rugby as the Maui dolphin and the Kakapo parrot, which makes Mike Blair a unique individual in the Land of the Long White Cloud.

Speaking on the BBC Scotland Rugby Podcast, Blair describes his new life as Dave Rennie's attack coach with the All Blacks, a high-profile and high-pressure job, a unique honour, all the more welcome because Scottish coaches in elite rugby are desperately thin on the ground.

Rugby.summary: When the Ultimate Sevens Academy started back in 2013, few could have predicted that it would lead to a brand new global sevens competition.
Rugby.body:
When the Ultimate Sevens Academy started back in 2013, few could have predicted that it would lead to a brand new global sevens competition. It has been a long journey over the last 13 years, but the academy’s goal to develop sevens players in the UK has proven a fruitful one, expanding out into Europe and North America.

It has been at the crux of the development of the Ultimate Sevens, with Managing Director Barney Pascall excited to turn sevens into a supercharged pathway to get new fans and players into rugby, having started work with the academy in 2020.

Rugby.title: Fin Smith sets England autumn ultimatum to hit form
Rugby.summary: England fly-half Fin Smith says an under-par autumn would trigger fundamental questions about the team's direction.
Rugby.body:
England fly-half Fin Smith says an under-par autumn should trigger fundamental questions about the team's direction. The 24-year-old was asked by Rugby Union Weekly about the state of the team after a miserable Six Nations and a summer campaign that featured a 45-21 defeat by world champions South Africa, a 73-8 thrashing of Fiji and a narrow 31-24 win over Argentina.

"I am not going to sit here and say 'we are building' because that is what you will get every time. "We will honestly find out in the autumn. If we have a pretty ropey autumn, on the back of building some momentum over the summer, I think we will need to have a pretty hard look at ourselves."

Rugby.title: Olivia Apps: 'We rewatched the World Cup final
Rugby.summary: When Canada play England at Sandy Park this Saturday, it will be 357 days since the two teams met in the Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 final.
Rugby.body:
When Canada play England at Sandy Park this Saturday, it will be 357 days since the two teams met in the Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 final. It is a day that will live in the memory of rugby supporters for plenty of years, as 81,885 supporters piled in to Allianz Stadium to conclude the best-attended and most successful edition of the tournament ever.

While the memory is bright for many, for Canada, the memory carries a little more darkness. Beaten 33-13 in West London the side left the field knowing that they did not live up to the potential they had shown in the lead-up to the final.

Tennis.summary: Carlos Alcaraz discusses his US Open return, why he "misses" rival Jannik Sinner and his excitement for this year's Laver Cup.
Tennis.body:
Most players, after seeing their US Open title defence end at 3.34am after five intense sets, would not walk away smiling. After his loss to Ben Shelton - a match that played out over a gruelling four hours and 28 minutes - the Spaniard was filmed walking down the Arthur Ashe tunnel with a huge grin on his face.

Alcaraz had been competing in his first tournament for over five months after suffering a wrist injury that left him in pain every day. He did not defend his French Open title or compete at Wimbledon, and did not know if he would play in New York until a week before.

Tennis.summary: Andy Murray set to face Rafa Nadal for first time in 10 years in Rafa Nadal Academy Slam Sky Sports

Tennis.title: Emma Raducanu: Andre Agassi is helping me out of my slump
Tennis.summary: Emma Raducanu: Andre Agassi is helping me out of my slump AOL.com
Tennis.body:
Emma Raducanu has been taking inspiration from Andre Agassi as she attempts to get back on track. Raducanu, who has faced a constant battle with injuries since her US Open triumph five years ago as a teenage qualifier, is reading the eight-time major winner’s 2009 autobiography and said the book was “so relatable”.

Agassi’s career has parallels with Raducanu’s given he was a teenage prodigy who quickly ascended to the top of the game. He claimed the first of his eight singles titles at Wimbledon in 1992, aged 22, but his career was later characterised by his challenges dealing with the crushing weight of expectation and drops down the rankings.

Tennis.title: Andre Agassi has advice for Emma Raducanu as her struggles continue over 2026
Tennis.summary: Andre Agassi has advice for Emma Raducanu as her struggles continue over 2026 Yahoo Sports
Tennis.body:
Andre Agassi has encouraged Emma Raducanu to be the "best of herself on a daily basis" amid her difficult 2026 season. Raducanu has slipped to 98 in the WTA rankings, with injuries limiting the former US Open champion to just 21 matches all season. She has dropped well below her career-high ranking of 10, and has really struggled to enjoy a consistent run of tournaments throughout 2026.

But in a bid to get back to her best, Raducanu has been taking inspiration from Agassi's 2009 autobiography. She has related to his success at an early age, with the Briton having lifted the US Open trophy as an 18-year-old. It represents her only WTA title. The American has now reached out to the 23-year-old, offering her advice on what she can do at this stage of her roller-coaster career.

Tennis.title: 'Be comfortable in your own identity'
Tennis.summary: As Emma Raducanu plots a route back to the pinnacle of tennis, the Briton is taking inspiration from Andre Agassi's 2009 autobiography.
Tennis.body:
As Emma Raducanu plots a route back to the pinnacle of tennis, the Briton has been taking inspiration from Andre Agassi's 2009 autobiography. Five years have passed since Raducanu's remarkable US Open triumph, when at the age of 18 she became the first qualifier in the Open era to win a Grand Slam.

American Agassi was a teenage prodigy himself and later claimed the first of his eight major singles titles at Wimbledon in 1992 aged 22. But between the peak years of his career, he had to overcome a challenging period when he went four years without a major and dropped to 141st in the world rankings.

Tennis.title: Banned Moore's £15m lawsuit against WTA dismissed
Tennis.summary: British player Tara Moore's legal bid for £15m in damages over a doping case which led to her being banned for four years is dismissed.
Tennis.body:
British doubles player Tara Moore's legal bid for £15m ($20m) in damages from the Women's Tennis Association - over a doping case which led to her being banned for four years - has been dismissed by a United States court.

Moore, 34, argued the WTA - the governing body of the women's tour - failed to warn players about the risk of eating contaminated meat at a tournament held in Colombia. But the United States District Court in New York has dismissed Moore's motion and directed to "close this matter".

Tennis.title: Keothavong 'can't fault' GB after BJK Cup loss to Czechs
Tennis.summary: Sonay Kartal and Katie Boulter lose their singles matches as Great Britain are beaten by a strong Czech Republic side in the Billie Jean King Cup quarter-finals.
Tennis.body:
Great Britain captain Anne Keothavong says she "cannot fault" her team's efforts after they were beaten by a strong Czech Republic side in the Billie Jean King Cup quarter-finals.

Keothavong's team headed into the tie as underdogs, with all five Czech players placed higher in the singles rankings than any of the British squad. Sonay Kartal produced a gritty performance as she returned to tennis after six months out with a lower back injury, but fell to a narrow 7-6 (7-2) 4-6 6-4 defeat in a marathon three-hour encounter with Marie Bouzkova.

Tennis.title: Billie Jean King Cup: Great Britain knocked out at quarter-final stage vs Czech Republic as Katie Boulter, Sonay Kartal beaten

Great Britain's stay at the Billie Jean King Cup Finals lasted only one match as they fell to Czechia in the quarter-finals in Shenzhen. Anne Keothavong's side were bidding to reach the last four for the fourth time in five years but were considerable underdogs and defeats for Sonay Kartal and Katie Boulter sealed their fate.

Led by Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova, the whole Czech team is ranked higher than any of Britain's players, and it was Noskova who sealed victory with a 6-2 7-6 (7-3) win over Boulter.

Tennis.title: Davis Cup: Great Britain book place in Finals as Neal Skupski and Henry Patten victory over Ecuador
Tennis.summary: Davis Cup: Great Britain book place in Finals as Neal Skupski and Henry Patten victory over Ecuador Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Great Britain wrapped up a straightforward victory over Ecuador to book their place at the Davis Cup Finals in November. After singles victories for Arthur Fery and Toby Samuel on Saturday at London's Copper Box, Henry Patten and Neal Skupski clinched the tie at the earliest opportunity with a 6-3 6-4 win against Gonzalo Escobar and Diego Hidalgo in the doubles rubber.

Britain therefore join three-time defending champions Italy, Canada, Czech Republic, South Korea and Austria in booking their spot for the eight-team event in Bologna. It is the first time Leon Smith's side have reached the quarter-finals since 2023, when they were beaten by Novak Djokovic's Serbia in Malaga.

Tennis.title: GB dominate Ecuador to reach Davis Cup Finals
Tennis.summary: Great Britain will play in the Davis Cup Finals for the first time since 2023 after claiming a 4-0 win against Ecuador in London.
Tennis.body:
Great Britain have reached the Davis Cup Finals for the first time since 2023 after sealing a 4-0 win in their qualifying tie against Ecuador. Henry Patten and Neal Skupski booked Britain's ticket to November's 'Final 8' event in Bologna with a 6-3 6-4 win over Gonzalo Escobar and Diego Hidalgo in the doubles at London's Copper Box Arena.

That gave Britain an unassailable 3-0 lead after wins on Saturday for Toby Samuel and Arthur Fery in the singles, before Harry Wendelken, a late call-up to the team after Cameron Norrie withdrew injured on Friday, wrapped up the best-of-five tie by beating Angel Veliz 6-2 6-3 on his competition debut.

Tennis.title: Hewett & Reid star as GB win fifth World Team Cup
Tennis.summary: Great Britain become World Team Cup champions for the fifth time as Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid secure a 2-1 victory over Japan in Florida.
Tennis.body:
Great Britain became World Team Cup champions for the fifth time as Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid joined forces to secure a 2-1 victory over Japan in Florida. Japan were the defending champions of the competition, which is the wheelchair tennis equivalent to the Davis Cup and Billie Jean King Cup.

However, Hewett and Reid ensured Britain got their hands back on the trophy with a 6-1 6-2 win in the deciding doubles match against Tokito Oda and Daisuke Arai. "We're really happy to get the title back," said Reid, who was also part of the World Team Cup-winning squad alongside Hewett in 2015, 2019, 2023 and 2024.

Tennis.title: She is the only player Emma Raducanu has beaten at a Grand Slam this year after missing Wimbledon and the US Open
Tennis.summary: She is the only player Emma Raducanu has beaten at a Grand Slam this year after missing Wimbledon and the US Open Yahoo Sports
Tennis.body:
Emma Raducanu will want to forget her 2026 Grand Slam season in a hurry. Raducanu won the US Open in 2021, becoming the first and only qualifier to win a Grand Slam title. The Briton has dealt with many injury issues since then, with a stress fracture in Raducanu's lower right leg forcing her to miss both Wimbledon and the US Open.

Raducanu also lost in the first round of Roland Garros this year, with her only Grand Slam victory coming at the Australian Open back in January. Raducanu came into this year's Australian Open with little expectation, as a foot injury had hampered her preparations for the new season.

Tennis.title: Jack Draper's season-ending news is disappointing but might save his future
Tennis.summary: Jack Draper's season-ending news is disappointing but might save his future Lob and Smash
Tennis.body:
Jack Draper simply needs a break, but the question is how long his body forces him to be away from tennis. The 24-year-old Brit has called it a season, about a month before his 2026 season would have ended anyway. Will he be able to come back healthier in 2027? Maybe not.

His longest-term injury is to his left arm (Draper's dominant hand), and it is an unusual bone. He has chronic bruising from internal bleeding in his humerus. The ailment forced him to miss every Grand Slam event this year, and his former top-10 ranking has fallen all the way to No. 143.

Golf.title: Fred Couples had a hunch. For U.S., it resulted in something special
Golf.summary: At the Presidents Cup on Wednesday, Xander Schauffele and Patrick Cantlay explained Fred Couples’ role in their team-event partnership. The post Fred Couples had a hunch. For U.S., it resulted in something special appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
One of the first times Xander Schauffele and Patrick Cantlay spent quality time together was over an intense game of gin rummy en route to the 2019 Presidents Cup in Australia. The U.S. team’s 26-hour charter from the Bahamas to Melbourne afforded the Presidents Cup rookies plenty of time to bond, and bond Schauffele and Cantlay did — over sets, runs and exchanging of dollars. The spark between the two players did not escape U.S. team vice-captain Fred Couples.

In Schauffele and Cantlay, Couples saw more than just budding pals — he saw a budding partnership. “Freddy [was] like, ‘Hey, I think these two guys would be unbelievable together,’” Schauffele said Wednesday from this year’s Presidents Cup at Medinah Country Club outside Chicago. “The way they play, they almost turn into one person when they’re playing alternate shot, which is all you can sort of ask for. And then just the way we interact. Holding each other accountable, but knowing that each of us are trying our absolute hardest on every shot. Just having each other’s back. Freddy sort of orchestrated that, and he was right.”

Golf.title: How to easily execute a longer greenside bunker shot
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Sarah Stone explains the keys to executing a long greenside bunker shot just like the pros do. The post How to easily execute a longer greenside bunker shot appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
With the Presidents Cup coming to Medinah Country Club and the recent redesign of the greenside bunkering, we’re likely to see the world’s best players faced with longer, more challenging bunker shots. Most golfers have an easier time mastering a short bunker shot 10-15 yards from the pin, but struggle when they are faced with a longer bunker shot.

The good news is that these longer bunker shots don’t have to be complicated. You generally have enough distance to launch the ball with some carry without having to hit a high, soft shot like you would on a shorter bunker shot.

Golf.summary: Fans rooted against Wyndham Clark during his 2026 U.S. Open win. Now he's hoping the U.S. fans have his back at the 2026 Presidents Cup. The post ‘Media has made me out to be villain’: Major champ hopes to avoid hecklers at Presidents Cup appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Will the Chicago golf fans be kinder to Wyndham Clark than the Long Island fans were to him in June? That’s one question on the mind of the two-time major champion as the 2026 Presidents Cup gets underway at Medinah.

This summer, Clark fought through final-round struggles to win the 2026 U.S. Open at Shinnecock Hills. But he didn’t just fight his game in the final round. He also had to contend with unruly fans, many of whom were openly rooting against him as he battled for his second victory in America’s national championship.

Golf.summary: The latest limited-edition Scotty Cameron putters are now available for pre-order: the Phantom 11R OC Spec III and the Phantom 5 OC Spec III. The post Limited-edition Scotty Cameron Phantom Spec III putters now available for pre-order appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The latest limited-edition Scotty Cameron putters are now available for pre-order at Fairway Jockey: the Phantom 11R OC Spec III and the Phantom 5 OC Spec III. The Phantom 11R OC Spec III is a high-MOI model with a tour-inspired, rounded shape, while the Phantom 5 OC Spec III features a compact, modern wingback head shape. Both models feature three high-contrast sightlines on the putterhead to help you lock in your start line, as well as chain-link face milling, which provides a responsive, soft feel and sound at impact.

Both limited-edition Phantom models feature a physical vapor deposition (PVD) finish that bonds to the milled head, resulting in an eye-catching dark black look that eliminates glare at address, as well as Scotty Cameron’s Onset-Center (OC) configuration, in which a straight shaft is installed directly in line with the putter’s CG, with a one-degree forward shaft lean, enabling players to employ a twist-resistant and simplified square-to-the-path stroke.

Golf.title: I asked a Tour coach to fix my putting. He made 2 simple fixes
Golf.summary: GOLF.com game-improvement editor Zephyr Melton did a putting fundamentals bootcamp with Tour coach Stephen Sweeney to fix his putting. The post I asked a Tour coach to fix my putting. He made 2 simple fixes appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
When I was a kid, putting was the strongest part of my game. I didn’t have unlimited access to a driving range, but the putting green was always free. So, after dinner most nights, I’d head over to the course and hit putts until the sun went down.

Now, as a 30-something living in New York City, I face the opposite obstacle. I can head to the simulator any time of day to work on my swing, but there aren’t many putting greens in my vicinity. So naturally, I’m now a much better ball-striker than putter.

Golf.body:
What I’m about to say is going to make me sound like a golf dinosaur: Until last month, I had never used a handheld rangefinder. Shocker, I know! But the devices just never seemed to jibe with me.

In my junior golf days, like our forefathers from generations past, I calculated yardages the old-fashioned way, by pacing them off, using fairway monuments and sprinkler heads. As I got older, I utilized digital golf-cart screens or mooched off a playing partner who had a rangefinder and was willing to zap the pin for me.

Golf.title: What you can learn from the pros' tee shots at the Presidents Cup
Golf.summary: Eva Rogers, a teaching pro at Medinah Country Club, explains how watching pros' tee balls at the Presidents Cup can be a learning experience. The post What you can learn from the pros’ tee shots at the Presidents Cup appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
With the Presidents Cup coming to Medinah Country Club, the strategy off the tee will be about much more than simply finding the fairway. The recent renovation by OCM Golf created areas of width that give players different ways to play a hole. A player can challenge the penal bunkers and potentially earn a better position for the next shot, or play to the safer side knowing they may be sacrificing distance or a more open angle into the green.

This multitude of options puts a premium on decision-making off the tee. Tour players know their carry distance, understand their normal dispersion and recognize how much of a bunker they can realistically challenge much better than most players, and with that premium skillset, it affords them plenty of options off the tee. Sometimes taking on more risk creates an advantage. Other times, choosing less club and keeping the most penal trouble out of play is the smarter decision.

Golf.body:
It’s the sort of question that seems dumb to ask. Is Scottie Scheffler — historically great World No. 1, good at everything, liked by everyone, long, straight driver, generational irons player, all-world chipper and underrated putter — tricky to pair up in team competition?!

Luckily somebody else asked it. And U.S. Presidents Cup captain Brandt Snedeker acknowledged that, yeah, in fact, it actually is. I appreciated Snedeker engaging with the question. These team match-play competitions are, to an extent, flukey one-offs, to the point that you can issue a hand-wave dismissal of basically any result (“they just made more putts,” the losing team tends to say with a shrug), which is always tough to refute but also isn’t particularly interesting.

Golf.title: Amid golf-ball rollback debate, USGA and R&A propose 3 new rules
Golf.summary: The golf-ball rollback is delayed for now, but governing bodies are considering near-term solutions for January 2028. The post Amid golf-ball rollback debate, USGA and R&A propose 3 new rules appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Golf’s ongoing rollback debate has taken its latest turn. Earlier this week, the USGA and R&A sent out their fourth notice of 2026 to manufacturers regarding potential solutions to increasing distances at golf’s highest levels. This time, the governing bodies are seeking feedback on three potential model local rules (MLR) that could slow the rapid gains in distance while the rulesmakers continue to consider a proposed golf-ball rollback.

The three potential MLRs were suggested by the PGA Tour and DP World Tour, which began working in consultation with the USGA and R&A in June, when the four organizations jointly announced the delayed implementation of any proposed golf-ball rollback.

Golf.summary: J.J. Spaun was among the players left off Brandt Snedeker’s Presidents Cup team. On Tuesday, Snedeker delivered Spaun and Co. a message. The post ‘Make me look stupid’: Presidents Cup snubs get message from U.S. captain appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The 12th-ranked male golfer in the world will be watching the Presidents Cup from home this week. That would be J.J. Spaun, the 2025 U.S. Open champion, who received a bad-news call from U.S. captain Brandt Snedeker on Monday of last week.

“A 45-second phone call,” is how Spaun described the exchange. “Just said I wasn’t on the team, and said I was the odd man out, and I wished him luck and that was it.” Perceived snubs are an inevitable part of any team selection that includes a captain’s input. When subjectivity enters the process, so, too, do sour feelings. Happens at the Ryder Cup, the Solheim Cup, the Walker and Curtis cups — and, yep, the biennial Presidents Cup, which this week visits Medinah Country Club near Chicago.

Golf.title: Scottie Scheffler airs frustration over U.S. team false 'narratives'
Golf.summary: As Scottie Scheffler and Team USA try to solve his match-play question, the post-Ryder Cup narratives have frustrated him and his teammates. The post Scottie Scheffler airs frustration over U.S. team false ‘narratives’ appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Scottie Scheffler hasn’t looked like Scottie Scheffler in this arena. The world No. 1 has lorded over the golf universe for the last four years. Roll the balls out in a 72-hole stroke-play event, and chances were good that by Sunday night Scheffler would’ve found himself either holding the trophy or coming a whisker shy. Ask anyone in pro golf, from Rory McIlroy to Jordan Spieth, and the answer is the same: It’s Scottie Scheffler . . . and everyone else.

But that hasn’t been the case in weeks like this one at the Presidents Cup, where Scheffler’s normally inevitable greatness has not arrived in the match-play format. In two previous Presidents Cups, Scheffler is 3-5-1 overall with a 1-3-1 record in foursomes and a 0-2-1 record in singles. His numbers are just as confounding at the Ryder Cup, where he is 3-6-3 with a 0-4-0 record in foursomes and a 1-2-2 mark in fourball.

It has been almost 30 years since the Americans lost their only Presidents Cup and 23 years since the last time the Internationals didn’t take an L (2003 ended in a tie). There have been a few close matches, but for the most part, the Americans overwhelm the Internationals every two years with their depth. The Americans are expected to win and win big at Medinah, but the Internationals, led by captain Geoff Ogilvy, believe they have the ingredients to keep it close and give themselves a chance to pull off a historic upset come Sunday.

Team competitions always bring drama, second-guessing and pressure, the latter of which will be everywhere this week at Medinah as the Americans try to extend their winning streak and the Internationals try to flip the script of a one-sided event.

Golf.title: Presidents Cup preview: 7 things to know about Medinah Country Club
Golf.summary: This week's Presidents Cup at Medinah will take place on a course that has proved its mettle in multiple big-time tournament tests. The post Presidents Cup preview: 7 things to know about Medinah Country Club appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Justin Rose, Ian Poulter and their European teammates pulled one off with a stunning Sunday comeback at the 2012 Ryder Cup. Now, nearly a decade and a half later, must-watch match play is returning to the scene of that shocker, Medinah Country Club, outside Chicago. This time it’s the Presidents Cup, 12 Americans against 12 Internationals on the club’s No. 3 course. Given the historical record — the U.S. owns a lopsided 13-1-1 edge in this event — the Internationals will need some magic of their own. Here are seven things to know about the grounds where they’ll try to conjure it.

The club was founded in 1924 by a group of Shriners who belonged to the Medinah Temple in Chicago, which itself was named for the holy city of Medina in Saudi Arabia. The distinctive architecture of the clubhouse, replete with domes and minarets, reflects that Middle Eastern etymology.

Golf.title: Srixon rethought its whole process for new ZXi RKT metalwoods
Golf.summary: The Srixon ZXi RKT drivers, fairway woods and hybrids are the result of a whole new development process that has already yielded a major win. The post Srixon rethought its whole process for new ZXi RKT metalwoods appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Srixon isn’t just announcing a new lineup of drivers; it’s a complete overhaul of how the company thinks about metalwoods. The new ZXi RKT line of metalwoods is the product of a brand new development process for Dunlop Sports (the parent company of Cleveland, Srixon and XXIO), which is now focusing on the Srixon brand as their main platform for metalwoods and irons.

“It was overall just like rethinking how we design woods and getting it more geared towards this market and kind of the PGA players,” Patrick Ripp, Srixon’s Tour Engineering Manager, told GOLF. “From there, we developed a whole Tour prototyping team and a lot of the engineers that work on that, were working with the Tour and other products and had good relationships with the players and good relationships with the reps and really just started solving the problems that we had seen.”

Golf.title: 2026 Presidents Cup rosters, records: Meet the U.S., International teams
Golf.summary: The 2026 Presidents Cup begins Thursday, September 24. View the U.S. and International team rosters and records here. The post 2026 Presidents Cup rosters, records: Meet the U.S., International teams appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
From left to right: Hideki Matsuyama, Sungjae Im, Scottie Scheffler and Russell Henley at the 2024 Presidents Cup. All four players are back again to battle at Medinah. The 16th Presidents Cup tees off this week at famed Medinah Country Club in Illinois, located approximately 30 miles northwest of downtown Chicago. The biennial event is yet another illustrious feather in Medinah’s host-course cap, adding to a resume that already includes three U.S. Opens (1949, 1975, 1990), two PGA Championships (1999, 2006), and a Ryder Cup (2012).

Heading into this week, the U.S. has a dominant 13-1-1 record over the Internationals since the event’s first playing in 1994. The Americans’ lone loss was the 1998 edition at Royal Melbourne GC, which the International team won by a score of 20.5-11.5. In 2003, the Presidents Cup was also famously tied with a score of 17-17 at Fancourt Hotel and Country Club in South Africa.

Golf.title: Inside Medinah Country Club's spectacular 100-year-old clubhouse
Golf.summary: Medinah Country Club's epic, century-old clubhouse still thrills, no matter how many times it has been experienced. The post Inside Medinah Country Club’s spectacular 100-year-old clubhouse appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Medinah Country Club in suburban Chicago is a shrine to golf, the host of three U.S. Opens (1949, 1975, 1990), two PGA Championships (1999, 2006), a Ryder Cup (2012) and this week, the Presidents Cup between the U.S. and International teams. It’s also a shrine to Shriners International, an American Masonic society known for its philanthropy, fellowship, fun — and red fezzes.

Shriners from Chicago’s Medinah Temple founded the club in 1924. The Shriners’ formal name, “Ancient Arabic Order of the Nobles of the Mystic Shrine,” helps explain why charter member and renowned architect Richard Gustav Schmid designed Medinah’s expansive, exquisite clubhouse in a Byzantine style, topped with minarets and classic Moorish architectural elements.

Golf.title: Rules Guy: Can I quickly mark a ball on a slope before it rolls back?
Golf.summary: If your ball is on a steep slope, can you mark it quickly to avoid it rolling backward? Rules Guy has the answer. The post Rules Guy: Can I quickly mark a ball on a slope before it rolls back? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The Rules of Golf are tricky! Thankfully, we’’e got the guru. Our Rules Guy knows the book front to back. Got a question? He’s got all the answers. If I hit a ball onto the green and it stops at the top of a slope, can my caddie run up and mark it before a gust of wind might make it roll back down the slope? – Rick Gacho, via email

Presumably you are tipping this looper well, yes? Indeed, your caddie — or even, dare we say, you — can run like the wind to prevent any breeze from blowing your ball away. Rule 14.1 gives a caddie the right to mark and lift a player’s ball on the putting green … assuming the ball hasn’t already started rolling. Just give him or her a little something, you know, for the effort.

Golf.title: Golf’s next megastar? And Miracle memories: 18 Presidents Cup thoughts
Golf.summary: Here are 18 Presidents Cup thoughts before the event at Medinah. Will Jackson Koivun take another step? Will 2012 be a story? And more. The post Golf’s next megastar? And Miracle memories: 18 Presidents Cup thoughts appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
MEDINAH, Ill. — Michael Phelps and I high-fived. Fourteen years ago here, at Medinah Country Club, swimming’s greatest of all time had been following the 2012 Ryder Cup from inside the ropes when his arms started working harder than they would in any pool. The Americans were surging at the finish of day one, and Phelps was slapping hands with anyone he could find to the left of the 17th hole — and his paw hit mine. It was a moment. I remember it. He sure as hell doesn’t. But I’m pretty sure we both left thinking Team USA would win, and I’m pretty positive we thought that even more so the next day.

Three pals and I had driven in on Tuesday night of Cup week. The previous October, one of them told us he’d won a ticket lottery, and he planned everything over an email thread that included Ian Poulter’s name in the subject line and I’ll leave it at that. Entry for the week — for the week — was $680, and I think that gets you in for a day now. We saw a couple practice rounds. We stood near Michael Jordan at one point. Phelps and I connected. I couldn’t leave him hanging.

Golf.title: Peyton Manning's $100 golf bet with Tiger Woods revealed much about Tiger
Golf.summary: In case you needed another reason to never bet against Tiger Woods, Peyton Manning shared an epic story in a recent interview. The post Peyton Manning’s $100 golf bet with Tiger Woods revealed much about Tiger appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
With 15 major championships and 82 PGA Tour victories on his resume, Tiger Woods’ competitive prowess is already the stuff of legends. But that all-encompassing drive to win wasn’t just limited to recorded tournaments. As two-time Super Bowl champion and Pro Football Hall of Famer Peyton Manning recently explained to GOLF’s Michael Bamberger, Woods’ burning desire to beat his opponents extended to pro-ams too.

Manning sat down to chat with Bamberger over Zoom to talk about the tournament he’s chaired for six years but which has existed for 34: the Smith Cole, which is held at Cherry Hills Country Club and attracts pro-member teams from clubs like Cypress Point, Seminole, Augusta National and more, who are then paired with Cherry Hills pro-member teams for a three-day competition.

Rumors about Bryson DeChambeau’s future continue to swirl. Last week, reports surfaced that LIV Golf only has 35 days to resign star players in order to secure 2.0 funding. Instead, the current (former?) Crushers captain announced something entirely new:

Golf.title: Robert MacIntyre blasts ‘ridiculous’ rule that sent him spiraling
Golf.summary: Robert MacIntyre was none to pleased with an embedded-ball ruling he received at the BMW PGA Championship on Sunday. The post Robert MacIntyre blasts ‘ridiculous’ rule that sent him spiraling appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Robert MacIntyre couldn’t have asked for a better three-hole finish at the DP World Tour’s big-money BMW PGA Championship on Sunday. Birdie. Birdie. Eagle. The four-under blitz at Wentworth moved MacIntyre to three under for his round and 13 under for the week, good for a share of 10th place. Still, after signing his card, the combustible Scotsman wasn’t exactly all sunshine and rainbows.

He had a gripe to air, and air it he did, to The Scotsman’s Martin Dempster. MacIntyre, who is ranked 19th in the world, was still stewing from what he described as a “ridiculous” ruling on the 11th, a par-4 on which his drive had found the left-center of the fairway. When MacIntyre arrived at his ball, he found it plugged — or at least semi-plugged — in another player’s pitch mark. The good news for MacIntyre was that a 2026 rule change seemingly meant that he’d be afforded relief for his submerged ball. The bad news: Model Local Rule F-2 includes an exception: If a referee determines that the pitch mark has been repaired in some way, the player will not receive relief.

Golf.title: Jacob Bridgeman's clubs: Earns 2nd win of season with new TaylorMade driver

Golf.body:
Jacob Bridgeman geared up for his first Presidents Cup matches in the best way possible: by picking up his second PGA Tour win at the Biltmore Championship in Asheville, N.C. After winning the Genesis Invitational in February, Bridgeman’s bag remains largely unchanged with a few notable exceptions to the top of his bag.

While he won using last year’s TaylorMade Qi35 LS driver, Bridgeman switched to the new Qi4D driver at last month’s BMW Championship. He also switched shafts to the new Project X Titan Green, becoming the second player to win with the new Titan family after Wyndham Clark won three times with Titan Yellow, and first with Titan Green. The green is billed as the stiffest profile in the family.

Golf.title: Jacob Bridgeman's latest win couldn't have been any more 'different' than his first
Golf.summary: Everything about Jacob Bridgeman's second win was different from his hand-numbing maiden victory at Tiger Woods' event — except one thing. The post Jacob Bridgeman’s latest win couldn’t have been any more ‘different’ than his first appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Back in February, Jacob Bridgeman arrived at the 18th hole at Riviera Country Club on Sunday with his dreams in his grasp. He was leading the Genesis Invitational, Tiger Woods’ tournament, with one hole to play. His first PGA Tour win was within reach; he just needed to par the final hole to hold off a hard-charging Rory McIlroy.

In the end, Bridgeman, despite being unable to feel his hands, made a four-foot par putt to beat McIlroy by one and win his idol’s tournament. That win sparked a season for Bridgeman that saw him make 22 of 23 cuts, post 11 top-10s and finish fourth at the Tour Championship. All that led to Bridgeman being picked by captain Brandt Snedeker to represent Team USA at next week’s Presidents Cup.

Golf.title: Ex-pros dish on U.S. team golf failures: 'Overblown, overdone and overanalyzed'
Golf.summary: Several former PGA Tour pros opened up about the challenges facing U.S. team golf ahead of the 2026 Presidents Cup. The post Ex-pros dish on U.S. team golf failures: ‘Overblown, overdone and overanalyzed’ appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
PEBBLE BEACH, Calif. — Rocco Mediate is honest about his Ryder Cup future. Mediate knows his chances of a U.S. Ryder Cup team roster spot ended long ago — around the moment Tiger Woods’ final putt dropped in the Monday playoff of the 2008 U.S. Open. He never played on an American Ryder Cup team. Never competed for the stars and stripes. Never felt the pressure over a 6-footer to extend your match. And maybe that’s for the best.

“I would have been the antichrist,” he says with a grin. But Rocco knows golf. He’s played professionally for more than three decades, and has been obsessed with sport’s history and traditions for just as long. He might not know what it feels like to be inside the team room, but he knows that success and failure in golf are decided in unusual ways. And this week, at the PURE Insurance Championship out in Pebble Beach, he has some ideas on how the Americans can turn things around after consecutive Ryder Cup losses despite what many view as a talent advantage.

Golf.title: What average golfers can learn from Ryan Fox's swift pre-shot routine
Golf.summary: Ryan Fox won the 2026 Open Championship at Royal Birkdale — and he did so with one of the fastest pre-shot routines in golf. The post What average golfers can learn from Ryan Fox’s swift pre-shot routine appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
One of the biggest lessons recreational golfers can learn from Ryan Fox’s epic Open Championship win doesn’t lie in his swing, but rather in his process. Foxy’s mental coach, Karl Morris, boils it down to three key words: intention, attention and attitude.

Intention means being clear about the shot you’re trying to hit. Decide what you want the ball to do, then commit to that picture. Attention is about keeping your focus in one place. Instead of juggling swing thoughts, give your mind one key. Finally, attitude is how you respond after the shot. Fox showed remarkable acceptance throughout the Open, particularly after unlucky breaks.

Golf.summary: Trump Returns With Pro-Trump Golfer, Ex-Ice Hockey Star 조선일보
Golf.body:
U.S. President Donald Trump, who was spending time at the presidential retreat in Camp David, Maryland, near Washington, D.C. over the weekend, suddenly returned to the White House at 8 p.m. on the 19th (9 a.m. Korean time on the 20th). As the State Department issued a new security alert on the same day urging heightened vigilance for Americans in the Middle East, various interpretations emerged regarding Trump’s early return, but the White House did not provide an answer. Trump is scheduled to attend several bilateral and multilateral events next week in conjunction with the UN General Assembly in New York.

On that day, the presidential helicopter ‘Marine One’ carrying Trump landed at the South Lawn in front of the White House, and inside the helicopter, golfer Bryson DeChambeau and Mikayla Demeita, a former Canadian ice hockey player, were captured on camera. DeChambeau, who is active in LIV Golf sponsored by Saudi Arabia, is a prominent pro-Trump figure in the golf world. Immediately after winning the 2024 election, he celebrated Trump on stage wearing a MAGA (Make America Great Again) hat. Trump also appeared directly on DeChambeau’s YouTube channel. In July, during the British Open, a major tournament, DeChambeau protested a two-stroke penalty and mentioned, “I will call President Trump,” sparking controversy.

Golf.title: The surprising memories lingering from Tiger Woods' history-changing Pebble Beach blowout
Golf.summary: Tiger Woods' 2000 U.S. Open will celebrate its 27th birthday next June, but it remains at the top of mind for the players he beat. The post The surprising memories lingering from Tiger Woods’ history-changing Pebble Beach blowout appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
PEBBLE BEACH, Calif. — Ernie Els laughs as the question arrives. Of course he remembers. You remember your great moments at the major championships like you remember your loved ones. When you have a score better than 154 players in the field at the U.S. Open, you don’t forget it.

But Els also laughs because he knows nobody has really thinks about his better-than-154-players score at the 2000 U.S. Open at Pebble Beach. They think only about the name that appeared above Els’ on the enormous manual scoreboard on 17 Mile Drive on that June Sunday — Woods. And yes, they think about how the only guy Ernie Els didn’t beat changed golf forever.

Golf.title: Rory McIlroy's electric eagle finish put much more than BMW PGA title in his sights
Golf.summary: With a show-stopping finishing eagle on Saturday, Rory McIlroy has the BMW PGA title and much more in his sights on Sunday. The post Rory McIlroy’s electric eagle finish put much more than BMW PGA title in his sights appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Rory McIlroy said he’d need to do something special. After a scruffy week in his title defense at the Irish Open, McIlroy arrived at this week’s BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth in second place in the Race to Dubai standings, giving himself a real chance to win his eighth season-long title this fall and tie Colin Montgomerie’s record of eight Race to Dubai crowns. But while McIlroy is in second place, he’s almost 1,000 points behind Patrick Reed, who won twice earlier this year.

“Obviously I’m in a very fortunate position, I guess, to be going for an eighth Race to Dubai. I can’t believe I’m sitting here with seven. So, yeah, I’d love to give myself a chance again,” McIlroy said in his pre-tournament press conference. “Last week wasn’t a great week for me in terms of the overall points. Patrick had a good week, and I didn’t have such a great week. I’m going to try — I’m going to have to try to make up for that this week.”

Golf.title: At Biltmore, 2 dream weeks are unfolding. Only 1 can end that way
Golf.summary: Neal Shipley and Ben Kohles are both hunting career-changing wins at the Biltmore. But only one can reach their dream ending on Sunday. The post At Biltmore, 2 dream weeks are unfolding. Only 1 can end that way appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
When Neal Shipley’s week began, his goal for the PGA Tour’s FedEx Cup Fall slate was clear: put the pedal down if he wanted to keep his card and playing privileges in 2027. Shipley, 25, became a sensation when he notched low amateur honors at the 2024 Masters and starred in an episode of Netflix’s docuseries Full Swing. Since that week at Augusta, which included a final-round pairing with Tiger Woods, Shipley has been grinding his way to the PGA Tour. Last year, he won twice on the Korn Ferry Tour to finish fourth in the standings and punch his ticket to pro golf’s big time. But his rookie season has been far from what he imagined. He missed 9 of his first 10 cuts and only made 8 of 20 cuts in total. He did not record a top-25 finish on the season and entered this week’s Biltmore Championship in Asheville, N.C., — the first tournament of the FedEx Cup Fall season — sitting at 183 in the FedEx Cup standings.

Needing to finish in the top 100 to keep his card, Shipley faced a steep uphill climb to remain on the PGA Tour in 2027. The math was clear: he needed either to post several high finishes or win between now and the RSM Classic in mid-November. Otherwise, he would be headed back to the Korn Ferry Tour.

Golf.title: How can playing golf alone help your game? This book seeks to find out
Golf.summary: In author Gary Belsky's new book "Solo Golf," he seeks to find out how playing golf alone can help your game. The post How can playing golf alone help your game? This book seeks to find out appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
In an era dominated by optimization, playing golf alone offers something increasingly rare: unstructured learning. Solo golf pares the game down to its essentials. And without distractions, a golfer becomes more attuned to the game.

As Gary Belsky writes in his new book, Solo Golf: The Zen of Playing Alone and How It Can Transform Your Game, solitude creates a different relationship with golf — one rooted in mindfulness and experimentation. A solo round turns the course into a laboratory.

Golf.title: 10 surprising players already qualified for 'new' PGA Tour
Golf.summary: The 'new' PGA Tour system doesn't start until 2028, but dozens of pros are already qualified — and a few more are in limbo. The post 10 surprising players already qualified for ‘new’ PGA Tour appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Earlier this week, the PGA Tour rolled out its eligibility criteria for its revamped two-tier system launching in 2028. The top-tier “Championship Series” will feature fields of roughly 120 players and there will be cut-and-dry promotion and relegation at the end of each season.

In other words, things will be simple. They just aren’t just yet. One surprising thing is just how many players have already secured their spots in the 2028 season. Because this is happening in real time, some exemptions are being grandfathered in, which makes the details of the “transition year” that much more compelling. Even ignoring the “Career Milestone” category (more on that later) there are roughly 40 players already eligible. Let’s run through 10 we know are in — plus a couple giant question marks — to make some sense of what’s to come.
